lead_en: Art starts with looking. This series begins with color, light, and line, and climbs one question at a time to space, materials, the many kinds of art, and the people who made it.
lead_zh: 美術從「看」開始。這個系列從顏色、光和線條講起，一次回答一個問題，一路講到空間、材料、美術的種類，以及創作的人。

intro.en: Every lesson has something you can move with your own hands: a lamp, a slider, a sheet of color. In Taiwan's school curriculum this subject is called Visual Arts. It is one of the three subjects in the Arts area, together with Music and Performing Arts.
intro.zh: 每一課都有可以自己動手的東西：一盞燈、一根滑桿、一片顏色。在十二年國教課綱裡，這個科目的正式名稱是「視覺藝術」，和音樂、表演藝術同屬藝術領域。

intro.en: A screen can only make light, so the paint on these pages is a drawing of paint, and each lesson says where the drawing is simplified. People do not all see color in the same way, so every color here also has a name, a letter, or a number beside it. When a later lesson shows a famous work, the image will come only from a museum that clearly releases it for open use.
intro.zh: 螢幕只會發光，所以這些頁面上的「顏料」是畫出來的示意，每一課都會說明它簡化了什麼。每個人看到的顏色不完全一樣，所以這裡的每一個顏色，旁邊都有名稱、字母或數字。之後的課若放名作，只用博物館明確開放使用的影像。

units.blurb_en: Color, light and shade, and line: the things your eyes work with before you draw anything.
units.blurb_zh: 顏色、明暗和線條：動筆之前，眼睛先要學會看的幾件事。

lessons.title: Why Do Paint and Light Mix Differently?
lessons.title_zh: 顏料和光，混色為什麼不一樣？
lessons.blurb_en: Shine a red, a green, and a blue lamp on a white wall and watch the overlaps turn yellow, cyan, magenta, and white. Then swap the lamps for three sheets of paint and see the overlaps get darker.
lessons.blurb_zh: 把紅、綠、藍三盞燈打在白牆上，看重疊的地方變成黃、青、洋紅和白；再把燈換成三片顏料，看重疊的地方越來越暗。
lessons.big_idea_en: Light adds: every lamp you switch on sends more light to your eyes, so the mix gets brighter, and red, green, and blue together look white. Paint takes away: every layer absorbs some of the light, so the mix gets darker, and yellow, magenta, and cyan together look almost black.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 光是用加的：每多開一盞燈，進到眼睛的光就多一些，所以越混越亮，紅、綠、藍加在一起看起來是白色。顏料是用減的：每多一層顏料，就多吸掉一些光，所以越混越暗，黃、洋紅、青疊在一起接近黑色。

lab.title_en: Three Lamps in a Dark Room
lab.how_en: Three lamps, one red, one green, and one blue, shine on a white wall. Drag a spot of light to move it. On the right you can switch each lamp off or make it dimmer, and read the name and the numbers of each color. Then press Paint: the same wall gets three sheets of paint instead, in yellow, magenta, and cyan. Every color on the wall has a label, so you never have to tell colors apart by eye alone.
lab.how_zh: 紅、綠、藍三盞燈照在一面白牆上。拖動光斑就能移動它；右邊可以把每一盞燈關掉或調暗，並讀出每個顏色的名稱和數值。再按「顏料」：同一面牆換成黃、洋紅、青三片顏料。牆上每個顏色都有標籤，不必只靠眼睛分辨顏色。

legend.en: A spot of light (or a sheet of paint); the label gives its letter and color name
legend.zh: 一個光斑（或一片顏料）；標籤寫著它的字母和顏色名稱

legend.en: An overlap; its label names the color that the mix makes
legend.zh: 重疊的地方；標籤寫的是混出來的顏色

legend.en: The small ring: the point whose color is read out on the right
legend.zh: 小圓圈：右邊讀出的是這一點的顏色

lab.scale_en: The numbers are screen values: R, G, and B each run from 0 (off) to 255 (as bright as the screen goes). The wall is drawn straight from those numbers, with no room lighting added.
lab.scale_zh: 數值是螢幕的設定值：R、G、B 各從 0（不亮）到 255（螢幕能顯示的最亮）。牆面直接照這些數字畫出來，沒有再加上房間的光影。
lab.note_head_en: What the paint model leaves out

notes.en: A screen can only make light. The sheets of paint here are drawn with red, green, and blue light, like everything else on your screen.
notes.zh: 螢幕只會發光。這裡的顏料色片，和螢幕上其他東西一樣，是用紅、綠、藍三種光畫出來的。

notes.en: The model cuts light into just three parts: red, green, and blue. Real light is a smooth spread of colors, and a real paint absorbs a little or a lot at every point along it.
notes.zh: 模型把光只切成紅、綠、藍三段。真正的光是連續的一整片顏色，真的顏料在每一段吸收的多寡都不一樣。

notes.en: The model treats paint as thin, clear sheets laid one over another, like colored film or printing ink. In paint that is stirred together, light meets many grains of pigment at different depths before it comes back out, so the result can differ.
notes.zh: 模型把顏料當成一片一片透明的薄片疊起來，像色片或印刷油墨。攪在一起的顏料裡，光要在不同深度碰到許多色料顆粒才出來，結果可能不一樣。

notes.en: How much each sheet absorbs (about nine tenths of one part of the light, and a little of the other two) are numbers we chose for this page. Nobody measured them from a real paint.
notes.zh: 每一片吸掉多少光（其中一段大約九成，另外兩段各一點點），是我們為這一頁選的數字，不是從真的顏料量出來的。

lab.note_end_en: So treat the paint side as a prediction, and test it with real paint. Classroom Activity 2 shows how.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請把顏料這一邊當成「預測」，再拿真的顏料來驗證；做法在課堂活動二。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn for this lesson. The color math is in a small color engine that later lessons share, and it is covered by automatic tests. · 模型為本課自行繪製；顏色的計算放在之後每一課共用的顏色引擎裡，並有自動測試。

paras: Squeeze yellow, magenta, and cyan paint onto a plate and stir them together. The mix turns into a dark gray that is close to black. Now go into a dark room with three lamps, one red, one green, and one blue, and point all of them at the same place on a white wall. That place turns white. Three colors of paint make something close to black, and three colors of light make white. Why are the two results opposite?

Start with the lamps. A wall in a dark room sends no light to your eyes. Switch on the red lamp, and the wall reflects red light back to you. Switch on the green lamp as well, and the place where the two spots overlap now reflects red light and green light together. More light reaches your eyes, so that place looks brighter, and it looks yellow. This is called additive mixing, because every lamp adds light. Red, green, and blue are called the primary colors of light. Red and green make yellow, green and blue make cyan, and red and blue make magenta. All three together make white.

Why yellow? The answer is in your eyes. At the back of each eye are cells called cones, and there are three kinds. Each kind responds to a wide range of light, but one is most sensitive to long waves, one to medium waves, and one to short waves. Your brain works out a color from how strongly the three kinds respond. A certain mix of red and green light stimulates the cones exactly as much as yellow light does, so your eyes cannot tell the two apart.

Paint does not make light. Paint gets its color from a pigment, and a pigment absorbs some of the light that falls on it and reflects the rest. White paper reflects almost all of the light. A layer of yellow paint absorbs most of the blue light. Magenta paint absorbs mostly green light, and cyan paint absorbs mostly red light. Lay yellow over magenta and both the blue and the green are taken away, so red is what is left. Each new layer takes away more light and the mix gets darker. This is called subtractive mixing.

Look again and you will see that the two sets fit together. Where two lamps overlap you get yellow, cyan, and magenta, and those are the three colors of paint in the model. Where two of those paints overlap you get red, green, and blue. A color printer uses cyan, magenta, and yellow ink for this reason. Real inks are not perfect, and the three together usually give a dark gray, so printers add black ink as well. A screen works the other way. Each pixel is usually made of three tiny lamps: one red, one green, and one blue.

In art class you may have learned a different set of primary colors: red, yellow, and blue. That set is older than modern color science, and it is still used in painting and in art lessons today. Printers use cyan, magenta, and yellow. Both sets are in use, and neither can do everything, because no three real paints, inks, or lights can mix every color there is. One more thing: the paint on this page is drawn by a screen, which means it is drawn with light. Try the same mixes with real paint and see how close the model comes.
paras_zh: 把黃、洋紅、青三種顏料擠在盤子上攪在一起，會變成接近黑色的深灰。現在走進一間暗房，拿紅、綠、藍三盞燈，全部照在白牆上的同一個地方，那個地方變成白色。三種顏料混出接近黑的顏色，三種光卻混出白色。為什麼結果剛好相反？
先看燈。暗房裡的牆不會把任何光送到你的眼睛。打開紅燈，牆就把紅光反射給你。再打開綠燈，兩個光斑重疊的地方同時反射紅光和綠光；進到眼睛的光變多了，所以那裡看起來更亮，而且是黃色。這叫做加法混色，因為每一盞燈都加上一些光。紅、綠、藍叫做色光三原色。紅加綠是黃，綠加藍是青，紅加藍是洋紅；三種全部加在一起是白色。
為什麼是黃色？答案在你的眼睛裡。眼睛後方有一種叫做視錐細胞的細胞，一共三種。每一種都對很大範圍的光有反應，但一種對長波的光最敏感，一種對中波，一種對短波。大腦根據這三種細胞反應的強弱判斷出顏色。某一種比例的紅光加綠光，刺激視錐細胞的程度和黃光一模一樣，所以眼睛分不出兩者的差別。
顏料不會發光。顏料的顏色來自色料，色料會吸收一部分照在上面的光，把其餘的反射出去。白紙幾乎把所有的光都反射出去。一層黃色顏料吸收大部分的藍光；洋紅色顏料主要吸收綠光，青色顏料主要吸收紅光。把黃色疊在洋紅上，藍光和綠光都被拿走，剩下的就是紅色。每多一層，被拿走的光就更多，混出來的顏色也更暗。這叫做減法混色。
再看一次，你會發現這兩組顏色剛好互相對應。兩盞燈重疊的地方是黃、青、洋紅，正是模型裡的三種顏料；其中兩種顏料重疊的地方，則是紅、綠、藍。彩色印表機用青、洋紅、黃三種墨水，就是這個道理。真正的墨水並不完美，三種疊在一起通常只是深灰，所以印表機還會加上黑色墨水。螢幕則反過來：每個像素通常由三個小小的燈組成，一個紅、一個綠、一個藍。
在美術課，你學到的三原色可能是另一組：紅、黃、藍。這一組比現代的色彩科學更早出現，今天的繪畫和美術課仍然在用；印刷則用青、洋紅、黃。兩組都有人用，也都不是萬能的，因為沒有任何三種真實的顏料、墨水或光，可以混出所有的顏色。還有一件事：這一頁的顏料是螢幕畫出來的，也就是用光畫出來的。請拿真的顏料混混看，看模型有多接近。
questions: On a white wall, why does the place where a red spot and a green spot overlap look brighter than the red spot alone?
Yellow paint over cyan paint looks green. Which light did each layer take away?
Why can a screen not show you exactly what real paint will do?
answers: The overlap reflects both the red light and the green light, so more light reaches your eyes there. Light mixes by adding, and every lamp you add makes the mix brighter.
The yellow layer absorbed most of the blue light and the cyan layer absorbed most of the red light. Green is the part of the light that neither layer took away.

A screen can only make light, so it draws paint with red, green, and blue light. The picture follows a simple model, and real paint behaves in more complicated ways. You have to mix real paint to find out.

vocab.exzh: 紅、綠、藍是色光的三原色。

vocab.exzh: 光的混色是加法的：每一盞燈都多加一些光。

vocab.ex: Mixing paint is subtractive: each layer takes some light away.
vocab.exzh: 顏料的混色是減法的：每一層都拿走一些光。

vocab.ex: Yellow paint absorbs most of the blue light.
vocab.exzh: 黃色顏料吸收大部分的藍光。

vocab.ex: White paper reflects almost all of the light that falls on it.
vocab.exzh: 白紙幾乎把照在上面的光全部反射出去。

vocab.ex: A pigment gives paint its color.
vocab.exzh: 色料讓顏料有了顏色。

vocab.ex: Where the red and green spots overlap, the wall looks yellow.
vocab.exzh: 紅色和綠色光斑重疊的地方，牆看起來是黃色的。

vocab.ex: Each pixel on the screen has a red, a green, and a blue part.
vocab.exzh: 螢幕上的每個像素都有紅、綠、藍三個部分。

What do red, green, and blue light make when all three are mixed at full brightness?

options: It absorbs most of the blue light and reflects the rest
It absorbs all of the light

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: One lamp, then two, then three
parts.text_en: Watch the lamps come on one at a time. Each overlap is brighter than the spots that make it, and the middle turns white.
parts.text_zh: 看三盞燈一盞一盞打開。每一塊重疊的地方都比原來的光斑亮，正中間變成白色。

parts.text_en: Full red with full green is yellow. With the green lamp at half, the same overlap is orange. The amounts matter as much as the colors.
parts.text_zh: 紅光全開加綠光全開是黃色；綠燈調到一半，同一塊重疊的地方變成橙色。各加多少，和加哪幾種一樣重要。

parts.meta_en: Put a ball in the light
parts.text_en: A ball blocks each lamp from a different side. Where only the red lamp is blocked, green and blue are left, and the shadow is cyan.
parts.text_zh: 一顆球從不同的方向擋住每一盞燈。只擋住紅燈的地方，剩下綠光和藍光，影子是青色的。

parts.text_en: The lamps become sheets of yellow, magenta, and cyan paint. Each new sheet takes more light away, and the middle is almost black.
parts.text_zh: 三盞燈換成黃、洋紅、青三片顏料。每多一片，就多拿走一些光，正中間接近黑色。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Can you make white with only two lamps? Can you make the middle of the paint lighter without taking a sheet away?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。只用兩盞燈，調得出白色嗎？不拿掉任何一片顏料，能讓正中間變亮嗎？

match.lead_en: Eight questions. In the first four you mix light: three sliders set the brightness of a red, a green, and a blue lamp. In the last four you mix paint: three sliders set how thick the yellow, magenta, and cyan layers are. Press Check to see how far apart the two colors are. Each slider then tells you, in words, whether it needs more or less.
match.lead_zh: 八道題。前四題混的是光：三根滑桿分別是紅、綠、藍三盞燈的亮度。後四題混的是顏料：三根滑桿分別是黃、洋紅、青三層顏料的厚度。按「對答案」看兩個顏色差多少；每根滑桿旁邊會用文字告訴你要多一點還是少一點。
match.note_en: The difference is a number called a color difference: 0 means the two colors are the same, and black and white are 100 apart. Here 6 or less counts as a match. The paint questions use the model above, so they are an illustration too.
match.note_zh: 「差多少」是一個叫做色差的數字：0 代表兩個顏色一樣，黑和白相差 100；這裡 6 以內就算調出來。顏料的題目用的是上面那個模型，所以同樣是示意。

zoom.lead_en: Pick a color, then drag the slider to magnify it. A screen has no white lamp and no yellow lamp. Each pixel is usually three small lamps side by side, red, green, and blue, and each one is set to its own brightness.
zoom.lead_zh: 選一個顏色，再拖動滑桿把它放大。螢幕裡沒有白色的燈，也沒有黃色的燈；每個像素通常是並排的三個小燈：紅、綠、藍，各自開到不同的亮度。
zoom.note_en: This is a drawing, not a photograph of your screen. Real screens arrange these small lamps, called subpixels, in more than one way, and some use four colors.
zoom.note_zh: 這是畫出來的示意，不是你的螢幕的照片。這些小燈叫做子像素（也有人叫次畫素）；真正的螢幕有不只一種排法，有些還用四種顏色。

primaries.en: Which Colors Are the Primary Colors?
primaries.lead_en: It depends on what you are mixing, and on who is doing the mixing. Three sets are in everyday use.
primaries.lead_zh: 要看你混的是什麼，也要看是誰在混。日常會遇到三套說法。

sets.where_en: Screens, stage lighting, and the lamps in this lesson.
sets.where_zh: 螢幕、舞台燈光，以及這一課的三盞燈。
sets.note_en: Additive: the mix gets brighter, and all three make white.
sets.note_zh: 加法混色：越混越亮，三種加起來是白。

sets.zh: 青、洋紅、黃（色料三原色，也叫印刷三原色）
sets.where_en: Color printers and printed books, with black ink (K) added: CMYK.
sets.where_zh: 彩色印表機和印刷品，再加上黑色墨水（K），合稱 CMYK。
sets.note_en: Subtractive: the mix gets darker. These are the colors you get where two of the lights overlap.
sets.note_zh: 減法混色：越混越暗。這三個顏色，正好是兩種色光重疊的地方出現的顏色。

sets.where_en: Paint boxes, color wheels, and many art lessons.
sets.where_zh: 顏料盒、色相環，以及許多美術課。
sets.note_en: Also subtractive, and older than modern color science. In 1725 the printmaker Jacob Christoph Le Blon wrote that all colors can be composed of yellow, red, and blue.
sets.note_zh: 同樣是減法混色，比現代的色彩科學更早出現。1725 年，版畫家勒布隆（Jacob Christoph Le Blon）寫道：所有的顏色都可以用黃、紅、藍三色配出來。

primaries.swatch_note_en: The swatches are screen colors chosen to stand for each name. They are not measurements of any ink or paint.
primaries.swatch_note_zh: 色塊是為了代表各個名稱而選的螢幕顏色，不是任何墨水或顏料的實測值。

points.en: The traditional set and the printing set are close relatives. The red-yellow-blue set can be considered an approximation of cyan-magenta-yellow. In the twentieth century, new synthetic pigments gave painters reds and blues that came closer to magenta and cyan.
points.zh: 傳統的一組和印刷的一組是近親。紅黃藍可以看成青、洋紅、黃的一種近似；到了二十世紀，新的合成色料讓畫家手上的紅和藍更接近洋紅和青。

points.en: No set of three real paints, inks, or lights can mix every color. Each set can reach some colors and misses others.
points.zh: 沒有任何三種真實的顏料、墨水或光，可以混出所有的顏色。每一組都有混得出來的顏色，也有混不出來的。

points.en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary lists them side by side. Its entry for 原色 gives red, green, and blue for light, red, yellow, and blue for paint, and adds that color printing often uses magenta, yellow, and cyan.
points.zh: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》把它們並列。「原色」一條寫的是：「紅、綠、藍是色光的三原色（疊加型）；紅、黃、藍是顏料的三原色（消減型），彩色印刷術中常用洋紅、黃、青作為三原色。」

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Colors · 顏色背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Three kinds of cones, a tartan ribbon, black ink, and the eyes of your classmates
culture_cards.title_zh: 三種視錐細胞、一條格子緞帶、黑色墨水，和同學的眼睛
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people worked out what color mixing is.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼弄懂混色的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: People normally have three kinds of cone cells, named L, M, and S for the long, medium, and short waves of light they are most sensitive to. Their strongest responses are at about 560, 530, and 420 nanometers. Each kind still responds to a wide range of light, and the ranges overlap. That is why three well-chosen lights are enough to make so many colors.
cards.body_zh: 人通常有三種視錐細胞，依照它們最敏感的長波、中波、短波的光，叫做 L、M、S。它們反應最強的地方大約在 560、530、420 奈米。不過每一種都對很大範圍的光有反應，範圍互相重疊。所以只要三種選得好的光，就能混出很多顏色。

cards.body_en: In 1861 the physicist James Clerk Maxwell gave a lecture about color at the Royal Institution in London. For it, the photographer Thomas Sutton photographed a tartan ribbon three times: once through a red filter, once through green, and once through blue. Put together again, the three pictures made one color image. The plates of that time hardly responded to red or green light, so the result was far from perfect. It is remembered as the first durable color photograph.
cards.body_zh: 1861 年，物理學家馬克士威（James Clerk Maxwell）在倫敦的皇家研究院做了一場關於顏色的演講。攝影師薩頓（Thomas Sutton）為這場演講，把一條蘇格蘭格子緞帶拍了三次：一次透過紅色濾鏡、一次綠色、一次藍色。三張照片再合在一起，就成了一張彩色影像。當時的感光版對紅光和綠光幾乎沒有反應，所以結果離完美還很遠；後人仍把它當作第一張能保存下來的彩色照片。

cards.k: In the Printer · 印表機裡
cards.zh: 印表機為什麼還要黑色墨水
cards.body_en: In theory, cyan, magenta, and yellow ink together absorb all the light. Real inks are not perfect, and the three together usually come out dark gray. Black ink covers those unwanted tints in the dark parts of a picture, keeps fine details sharp, and saves the more expensive color inks when only black or gray is needed. The K in CMYK stands for that black ink.
cards.body_zh: 理論上，青、洋紅、黃三種墨水疊在一起會吸掉所有的光。真正的墨水並不完美，三種疊起來通常只是深灰。黑色墨水可以蓋掉畫面暗處那些不該有的色偏、讓細節保持銳利，而且只需要黑或灰的地方，就不必用比較貴的彩色墨水。CMYK 的 K 指的就是這種黑色墨水。

cards.en: Not everyone sees the same colors
cards.zh: 每個人看到的顏色不完全一樣
cards.body_en: Some people's cones work differently, and reds and greens can be hard for them to tell apart. The U.S. National Library of Medicine says that among people of Northern European ancestry this affects about 1 in 12 males and 1 in 200 females, and fewer in almost all other groups studied. A study of school students in Kaohsiung from 2019 to 2021 found it in 3.46% of the boys and 0.14% of the girls. That is why this page writes a name or a letter beside every color.
cards.body_zh: 有些人的視錐細胞運作方式不同，紅色和綠色對他們來說不容易分辨。美國國家醫學圖書館的資料說，在北歐血統的族群裡，大約每 12 位男性、每 200 位女性有一位如此，其他被研究過的族群幾乎都比較少。2019 到 2021 年高雄市中小學生的一項研究裡，男生是 3.46%，女生是 0.14%。所以這一頁的每一個顏色，旁邊都寫了名稱或字母。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The arts curriculum and the science curriculum do not use the words for primary colors or color mixing. These are the closest entries. The links to color mixing are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 藝術領域和自然科學領域的課綱，都沒有出現「三原色」或「混色」這兩個詞。下面是最接近的條目；它們和混色的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 色彩感知、造形與空間的探索。
items.note_en: Sensing color is where this series begins.
items.note_zh: 「色彩感知」正是這個系列的起點。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Naming a color, and saying how it was mixed, is one way to recognize and talk about color.
items.note_zh: 說出一個顏色的名稱、說明它是怎麼混出來的，是辨識與溝通色彩的一種方式。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國中）
items.text: 色彩理論、造形表現、符號意涵。
items.note_en: Additive and subtractive mixing are part of color theory. The entry does not list them by name.
items.note_zh: 加法混色與減法混色屬於色彩理論，但這一條沒有點名。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 陽光是由不同色光組成。
items.note_en: This lesson runs it the other way: put colored lights together and you get white.
items.note_zh: 這一課反過來做：把幾種色光加在一起，得到白光。

items.text: 物體的顏色是光選擇性反射的結果。
items.note_en: This is the paint half of the lesson: a pigment absorbs some light and reflects the rest.
items.note_zh: 這是本課顏料那一半的依據：色料吸收一部分的光，反射其餘的。

myths.myth_en: Red, yellow, and blue are the only real primary colors.
myths.myth_zh: 只有紅、黃、藍才是真正的三原色。
myths.fact_en: Several sets are in use. Light is mixed from red, green, and blue. Printing uses cyan, magenta, and yellow. Painters have long used red, yellow, and blue. No set of three real paints, inks, or lights can mix every color.
myths.fact_zh: 通行的說法不只一套。光用紅、綠、藍來混；印刷用青、洋紅、黃；畫家長久以來用紅、黃、藍。沒有任何三種真實的顏料、墨水或光能混出所有的顏色。

myths.myth_en: The more colors you mix, the brighter the result.
myths.myth_zh: 混進去的顏色越多，結果就越鮮亮。
myths.fact_en: That holds for light, where each lamp adds more. With paint it runs the other way: each paint absorbs more of the light, so the mix gets darker.
myths.fact_zh: 光是這樣，因為每一盞燈都多加一些光。顏料正好相反：每一種顏料都多吸掉一些光，所以越混越暗。

myths.myth_en: A yellow patch on a screen sends out yellow light.
myths.myth_zh: 螢幕上黃色的地方，發出的是黃光。
myths.fact_en: On a typical screen, the red and green parts of each pixel are lit and the blue part is dark. No part is yellow. That mix stimulates your cones the way yellow light does, so you see yellow.
myths.fact_zh: 在一般的螢幕上，是每個像素的紅色和綠色部分亮著、藍色部分不亮，沒有任何一個部分是黃色的。這樣的組合刺激視錐細胞的方式和黃光一樣，所以你看到黃色。

myths.myth_en: A shadow is always gray or black.
myths.myth_zh: 影子一定是灰色或黑色的。
myths.fact_en: A shadow is a place that one light cannot reach. If other lights still reach it, you see their mix. Under red, green, and blue lamps, the shadow that blocks only the red lamp is cyan.
myths.fact_zh: 影子是某一道光照不到的地方。如果別的光還照得到，你看到的就是那些光混出來的顏色。在紅、綠、藍三盞燈下，只擋住紅燈的影子是青色的。

tricks.body_en: More lamps, brighter. More paint, darker.
tricks.body_zh: 燈越多越亮，顏料越多越暗。

tricks.title_en: RGB makes white, CMY makes almost black
tricks.title_zh: 紅綠藍變白，青洋紅黃接近黑
tricks.body_en: Three lights add up to white. Three paints take away nearly all the light.
tricks.body_zh: 三種光加起來是白色；三種顏料幾乎把光全部拿走。

tricks.body_en: Yellow absorbs blue, magenta absorbs green, and cyan absorbs red.
tricks.body_zh: 黃吸收藍，洋紅吸收綠，青吸收紅。

tricks.title_en: Two of one set make one of the other
tricks.title_zh: 這一組的兩個，混出那一組的一個
tricks.body_en: Red and green light make yellow. Yellow and magenta paint make red.
tricks.body_zh: 紅光加綠光是黃；黃色顏料加洋紅顏料是紅。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Do not look straight into a bright lamp or flashlight, and do not point one at anyone's eyes. Look at the wall, not at the lamp.
safety.zh: 不要直視很亮的燈或手電筒，也不要拿它照別人的眼睛。看牆面，不要看燈。

safety.en: Do not use a laser pointer for these activities. Taiwan's Bureau of Standards says a laser pointer must never be aimed at a person, least of all at the eyes, and that children under 14 should not use one.
safety.zh: 這些活動不要用雷射筆。經濟部標準檢驗局提醒：雷射筆不可對準人，尤其是眼睛，並禁止 14 歲以下兒童使用。

safety.en: Keep food and drinks away from the paint. Do not put paint, brushes, or painted fingers in your mouth, and wash your hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 食物和飲料不要放在顏料旁邊。顏料、畫筆和沾了顏料的手指都不要放進嘴巴；畫完要洗手。

safety.en: Before the room goes dark, clear the floor and decide where everyone will stand. Move slowly, and switch the room lights back on before you tidy up.
safety.zh: 關燈之前，先把地板清空，並決定每個人站在哪裡。慢慢走動；收拾之前先把教室的燈打開。

materials.en: Three flashlights of the same kind
materials.zh: 三支同一款的手電筒

materials.en: Red, green, and blue cellophane (or color filters) and rubber bands
materials.zh: 紅、綠、藍三種玻璃紙（或濾色片）和橡皮筋

materials.en: A white wall or a large sheet of white paper, in a room you can make dark
materials.zh: 一面白牆或一大張白紙，以及一間可以弄暗的教室

materials.en: A pencil or a finger to make shadows
materials.zh: 一支鉛筆或一根手指，用來做影子

steps.en: Cover each flashlight with one color of cellophane and hold it on with a rubber band. Use two layers if the color looks pale.
steps.zh: 每支手電筒各包一種顏色的玻璃紙，用橡皮筋固定。顏色太淡就包兩層。

steps.en: Darken the room. Shine each flashlight on the wall by itself and say its color.
steps.zh: 把教室弄暗。每支手電筒先單獨照在牆上，說出它的顏色。

steps.en: Overlap red and green. Before you look, say what you expect. Then try green with blue, and red with blue.
steps.zh: 讓紅光和綠光重疊。看之前先說出你的預測。再試綠加藍、紅加藍。

steps.en: Overlap all three. Move a flashlight nearer or farther to change how bright its spot is, until the middle looks as white as you can get it.
steps.zh: 三種光全部重疊。把某一支手電筒拿近或拿遠來改變光斑的亮度，直到中間盡量接近白色。

steps.en: Hold a pencil close to the wall in the white spot. Count the shadows and name their colors. Which lamp is blocked in each one?
steps.zh: 在白色光斑裡，把鉛筆拿到靠近牆面的地方。數一數有幾個影子，說出它們的顏色。每個影子裡，被擋住的是哪一支手電筒？

activities.tip_en: Cellophane is not a perfect filter, and flashlights are not equally bright, so your white may look a little pink or a little blue. That is normal. Compare what you see with the model on this page, and write down what is the same and what is different.
activities.tip_zh: 玻璃紙不是完美的濾色片，每支手電筒的亮度也不一樣，所以你的「白色」可能偏粉紅或偏藍，這很正常。把看到的結果和這一頁的模型比較，記下哪些一樣、哪些不一樣。

activities.title_zh: 螢幕和真的顏料比一比

materials.en: Watercolors: a yellow, a magenta or rose red, and a cyan or sky blue
materials.zh: 水彩：黃色、洋紅（或玫瑰紅）、青色（或天藍）各一

materials.en: The red and the blue from an ordinary paint box, to compare
materials.zh: 一般顏料盒裡的紅色和藍色，用來對照

materials.en: A brush, clean water, a plate, and white paper
materials.zh: 畫筆、清水、調色盤和白紙

materials.en: This page, with the model switched to Paint
materials.zh: 這一頁，並把模型切換到「顏料」

steps.en: In the model, look at the overlap of yellow and magenta. Write down the color name it shows. This is the prediction.
steps.zh: 在模型裡看黃色和洋紅重疊的地方，把它顯示的顏色名稱寫下來。這是「預測」。

steps.en: Paint a wide stripe of yellow on the paper and let it dry. Paint a stripe of magenta across it. Look at the square where they cross.
steps.zh: 在紙上畫一道寬寬的黃色，等它乾。再橫著畫一道洋紅。看兩道交叉的那一格。

steps.en: Do the same for yellow with cyan, for magenta with cyan, and for all three. Hold the paper beside the screen each time.
steps.zh: 黃加青、洋紅加青、三種全加，各做一次。每次都把紙拿到螢幕旁邊比較。

steps.en: Make a table with three columns: the mix, what the model showed, and what the paint did. Mark each row as close or not close.
steps.zh: 畫一張三欄的表：混了什麼、模型顯示什麼、顏料實際的結果。每一列註明「接近」或「不接近」。

steps.en: Now repeat the crossings with the ordinary red and blue in place of magenta and cyan. Which pair gives the cleaner green? The cleaner purple?
steps.zh: 把洋紅和青換成一般的紅色和藍色，再做一次交叉。哪一組混出來的綠比較乾淨？紫色呢？

activities.tip_en: Your results will not match the screen exactly, and they should not. The model leaves things out, every brand of paint is different, and a screen makes its colors with light. Finding where the model is wrong is the point of this activity.
activities.tip_zh: 你的結果不會和螢幕一模一樣，也不應該一樣：模型省略了一些事，每個牌子的顏料都不同，而且螢幕是用光來顯示顏色的。找出模型哪裡不準，正是這個活動的目的。

links_head.en: What light is, and what comes next

links.note_en: Sunlight is a mix of many colors, and the air scatters some of them more than others. That lesson is about light itself. This lesson does not repeat it.
links.note_zh: 陽光是許多顏色混在一起的光，空氣把其中一些顏色散射得比較多。那一課講的是光本身；這一課不再重複。

links.note_en: Raindrops spread white sunlight out into its colors. Here you did the opposite and put colored lights together.
links.note_zh: 雨滴把白色的陽光分散成各種顏色；這一課做的是反方向的事：把幾種色光加在一起。

links.note_en: The color wheel, neighbors and opposites, warm and cool colors, and a gray square that seems to change when its background does.
links.note_zh: 色相環、類似色與互補色、暖色與冷色，還有一塊會隨著底色「變色」的灰色方塊。

lessons.title: How Do Colors Work Together?
lessons.blurb_en: Pick a color on the wheel and watch one drawing change its mood as its colors change. Then find out why two squares of the very same gray can look different.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在色相環上選一個顏色，看同一張圖換了配色之後感覺怎麼變；再看看兩塊一模一樣的灰色，為什麼看起來會不一樣。
lessons.big_idea_en: You never see a color by itself. Neighbors on the color wheel are close to each other and look like one family. Colors on opposite sides differ the most and make each other stand out. Even the same gray looks lighter or darker depending on what is around it.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 我們從來不會單獨看到一個顏色。色相環上相鄰的顏色彼此接近，看起來像一家人；對面的顏色差最多，放在一起會互相襯托。就連同一個灰色，也會因為周圍的顏色不同，看起來比較淺或比較深。

lab.title_en: A Color Wheel and One Drawing
lab.title_zh: 一個色相環，和同一張圖
lab.how_en: Click a step on the wheel to make it the main color, marked with a star. Then choose how the other colors are picked: its neighbors, the color straight across, or three colors spaced evenly. The drawing on the right takes those colors. You can also change the wheel itself, from the painter's wheel to the screen wheel. Every step has a number, and the colors in use are named on the right, so you never have to tell them apart by eye alone.
lab.how_zh: 點色相環上的一格，把它設成主色（有星號的那一格）。再選其他顏色怎麼挑：它的鄰居、正對面的顏色，或平均分開的三個顏色。右邊那張圖會換上這些顏色。色相環本身也可以換：畫家的色相環，或螢幕的色相環。每一格都有編號，用到的顏色名稱列在右邊，不必只靠眼睛分辨。

notes.en: The twelve swatches on the painter's wheel are screen colors chosen to stand for the names. They are light from your screen, not paint, and no paint was measured to make them.
notes.zh: 畫家的色相環上那十二個色塊，是為了代表各個名稱而選的螢幕顏色。它們是螢幕發出的光，不是顏料，也不是從任何顏料量出來的。

notes.en: A wheel shows only hue. It cannot show how light or dark a color is, or how vivid or dull. Those need more room than a flat circle has.
notes.zh: 色相環只表示色相，沒辦法表示一個顏色有多亮多暗、多鮮豔或多混濁；那需要比一個平面的圓更多的空間。

notes.en: Twelve steps is a choice. Newton's circle had seven colors, Goethe's had six, and other wheels have more.
notes.zh: 分成十二格是一種選擇。牛頓的色環有七個顏色，歌德的有六個，也有分得更細的色相環。

notes.en: The number for how far apart two colors are comes from one formula. It is an estimate, and people's eyes do not all agree with it.
notes.zh: 兩個顏色「差多少」的數字來自一條公式，只是估計；每個人眼睛的感覺不一定和它一樣。

lab.note_end_en: So test what you see here with colored paper or paint. Both classroom activities show how.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請拿色紙或顏料來驗證這裡看到的結果；做法在兩個課堂活動裡。
lab.credit_html: Wheel and drawing made for this lesson. The color math is in the shared color engine and is covered by automatic tests. · 色相環與圖為本課自行繪製；顏色的計算放在共用的顏色引擎裡，並有自動測試。

paras: Cut two small squares from the same sheet of gray paper. Lay one on black paper and the other on white paper. Now they do not look the same. In 1810 the German writer Goethe noted that a gray shape on a black background looks much brighter than the same shape on white. Nothing happened to the paper. Your eyes and brain judge every color against the colors around it. This effect is called simultaneous contrast, and it is why artists think about colors in groups.

To plan those groups, artists bend the colors into a circle called a color wheel. Each place on the wheel is a hue, such as red, orange, or blue. Isaac Newton put the first color wheel in his book Opticks in 1704. In 1766 the English artist Moses Harris wrote about a wheel built on red, yellow, and blue, with orange, green, and purple between them. Painters still use a wheel like that one. Screens use another wheel, built on red, green, and blue.

Colors that sit next to each other on the wheel are called analogous colors. Red, red-orange, and orange are one example. Neighbors have a lot in common. A picture that uses an analogous color scheme looks like one family of color, with little contrast between its parts.

Colors on opposite sides of the wheel are called complementary colors. On the painter's wheel the pairs are red and green, yellow and purple, and blue and orange. Side by side they give a strong contrast. The French chemist Michel Eugène Chevreul studied this at the Gobelins tapestry works in Paris, where people had complained about the black dye. He found that the dye was good. The black only looked weak and reddish when deep blues surrounded it. A color, he wrote, seems to shift toward the opposite of its neighbor. He published his findings in 1839.

Which color is the opposite of red? It depends on the wheel. On the painter's wheel the answer is green. On the screen wheel the pairs are red and cyan, green and magenta, and blue and yellow. Both wheels are useful. One grew out of mixing paint and the other fits mixing light, as you saw in Lesson 1. When someone says two colors are complementary, it is fair to ask which wheel they mean.

Artists also call the hues from red through yellow warm, and the hues from blue-green through blue-purple cool. People have used these words since at least the late 1700s, but they do not agree on exactly where the line falls. You may also hear that warm colors excite people and cool colors calm them. Researchers who reviewed the studies say it is too early to make strong claims like that. The rules for matching colors are guides. They are not laws, and tastes differ from person to person and from culture to culture. Use the wheel to find ideas, and then trust what you see.
paras_zh: 從同一張灰色的紙上剪下兩個小方塊，一塊放在黑紙上，一塊放在白紙上。現在它們看起來不一樣了。1810 年，德國作家歌德記下：灰色的圖形放在黑色的底上，看起來比同一個圖形放在白色的底上亮得多。紙並沒有改變。眼睛和大腦判斷每一個顏色，都是拿它和周圍的顏色比較。這個現象叫做同時對比，也是藝術家總是把顏色一組一組來考慮的原因。
為了安排這些組合，藝術家把顏色彎成一個圓，叫做色相環。環上的每一個位置是一個色相，例如紅、橙、藍。牛頓在 1704 年出版的《光學》裡畫出了第一個色環。1766 年，英國藝術家哈里斯（Moses Harris）寫到一個以紅、黃、藍為基礎的色環，中間是橙、綠、紫。畫家到今天還在用類似的色相環。螢幕用的是另一個，以紅、綠、藍為基礎。
在色相環上相鄰的顏色叫做類似色，例如紅、紅橙、橙。鄰居之間有很多共同點。用類似色來配色的圖，看起來像同一家的顏色，各部分之間的對比很小。
在色相環上位置相對的顏色叫做互補色。在畫家的色相環上，這幾對是紅和綠、黃和紫、藍和橙。它們放在一起，對比很強。法國化學家謝弗勒（Michel Eugène Chevreul）在巴黎的戈布蘭織毯廠研究過這件事：當時有人抱怨那裡的黑色染料不好。他發現染料本身沒有問題，只是黑色被深藍色包圍的時候，看起來又淡又偏紅。他寫道：一個顏色看起來會偏向旁邊那個顏色的對面。他在 1839 年發表了這些發現。
紅色的對面是哪一個顏色？要看是哪一個色相環。在畫家的色相環上，答案是綠色。在螢幕的色相環上，這幾對是紅和青、綠和洋紅、藍和黃。兩個色相環都有用：一個是從混顏料發展出來的，另一個適合混光，就像第一課看到的那樣。有人說兩個顏色互補的時候，可以問一句：是哪一個色相環？
藝術家也把紅到黃的色相叫做暖色，把藍綠到藍紫的色相叫做冷色（也叫寒色）。這兩個詞至少從十八世紀後期就有人用了，不過交界線畫在哪裡，大家的說法並不一致。你可能也聽過「暖色讓人興奮、冷色讓人平靜」。整理過相關研究的學者說，現在要下這麼肯定的結論還太早。配色的規則是參考，不是定律；每個人、每個文化的喜好都不一樣。用色相環找靈感，然後相信自己看到的。
questions: Two squares cut from the same gray paper look different on black and on white. What changed, and what did not?
Why can two people both be right when one says the opposite of red is green and the other says it is cyan?
A friend says, "Blue always makes people calm." What would you say?
answers: The squares did not change. They are the same gray. What changed is the background, and our eyes and brain judge a color against the colors around it.
They are using different color wheels. On the painter's wheel, built on red, yellow, and blue, green is across from red. On the screen wheel, built on red, green, and blue, cyan is across from red.

It is a common saying, but researchers who reviewed the studies say it is too early for strong claims like that. People and cultures differ, so it is better to say that blue is usually called a cool color.

vocab.ex: On the color wheel, orange sits between red and yellow.
vocab.exzh: 在色相環上，橙色在紅色和黃色中間。

vocab.ex: Red, green, and blue are three different hues.
vocab.exzh: 紅、綠、藍是三個不同的色相。

vocab.ex: Yellow and yellow-green are analogous colors.
vocab.exzh: 黃色和黃綠色是類似色。

vocab.ex: On the painter's wheel, blue and orange are complementary colors.
vocab.exzh: 在畫家的色相環上，藍色和橙色是互補色。

vocab.ex: Black letters on white paper have a strong contrast.
vocab.exzh: 白紙上的黑字，對比很強。

vocab.ex: The gray square looks darker on a white background.
vocab.exzh: 灰色方塊放在白色的底色上，看起來比較深。

vocab.ex: She chose a color scheme of blue, blue-green, and green.
vocab.exzh: 她選了藍、藍綠、綠的配色。

vocab.ex: Red, orange, and yellow are called warm colors.
vocab.exzh: 紅、橙、黃叫做暖色。

quiz.q: What do we call colors that sit next to each other on the color wheel?
On the painter's wheel, built on red, yellow, and blue, which color is across from blue?
On the screen wheel, built on red, green, and blue, which color is across from red?
Two squares of the same gray sit on a black and a white background. Which one usually looks lighter?
Which hues are usually called warm colors?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the main color walk around the wheel with its two neighbors. The drawing changes color, but its parts always stay close to each other.
parts.text_zh: 看主色帶著兩個鄰居沿著色相環走一圈。圖的顏色一直在換，但各部分的顏色始終很接近。

parts.text_en: Blue with orange, red with green, yellow with purple. Each time the house and the hills pull apart, and the number on the right jumps up.
parts.text_zh: 藍配橙、紅配綠、黃配紫。每一次小屋和山丘都分得很開，右邊的數字也一下子變大。

parts.text_en: Keep red as the main color and change the wheel. Across from red is green on one wheel and cyan on the other.
parts.text_zh: 主色維持紅色，只換色相環。紅色的對面，在一個環上是綠色，在另一個環上是青色。

parts.text_en: The solid arc marks the hues usually called warm and the dashed arc the hues usually called cool. See the same drawing in three warm colors, then in three cool ones.
parts.text_zh: 實線的弧標出一般說的暖色，虛線的弧標出一般說的冷色。看同一張圖先用三個暖色，再用三個冷色。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Which scheme would you choose for a poster that must be seen from far away? Which for a quiet bedroom wall?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。一張要從遠處就看得到的海報，你會選哪一種配色？安靜的臥室牆面呢？

gray.eyebrow: See for Yourself · 自己看看
gray.lead_en: Two gray squares sit on two different backgrounds. Decide which one looks darker. Then slide the squares together, or give both sides the same background, and look again. The numbers under the picture tell you what the screen is really showing.
gray.lead_zh: 兩塊灰色的方塊放在兩種不同的底色上。先判斷哪一塊看起來比較深；再把兩塊移到一起，或把兩邊換成一樣的底色，再看一次。圖下方的數字告訴你螢幕實際顯示的是什麼。
gray.note_en: How strong the effect looks is different for each person and each screen. If you see no difference at all, that is fine too.
gray.note_zh: 這個效果看起來有多明顯，每個人、每個螢幕都不一樣。如果你完全看不出差別，那也沒有關係。

pick.lead_en: Six questions about the two wheels. Every choice shows a swatch and its name. The game counts the questions you get right on the first try. Watch for the last two: they ask the same thing as earlier questions, but on the other wheel.
pick.lead_zh: 六道關於兩個色相環的題目。每個選項都有色塊和名稱。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。留意最後兩題：問的是前面問過的事，只是換了一個色相環。
pick.note_en: You may scroll up and count the steps on the wheel. That is not cheating. It is how the wheel is meant to be used.
pick.note_zh: 可以捲回上面，在色相環上數格子。這不算作弊，色相環本來就是這樣用的。

wheels.en: The Color Across Depends on the Wheel
wheels.zh: 對面是什麼顏色，要看是哪一個色相環
wheels.lead_en: Start from the same color and cross each wheel. You land in two different places.
wheels.lead_zh: 從同一個顏色出發，分別走到兩個色相環的對面，會到達兩個不同的地方。
wheels.swatch_note_en: The swatches are screen colors chosen to stand for each name. The starting colors are the ones on the painter's wheel.
wheels.swatch_note_zh: 色塊是為了代表各個名稱而選的螢幕顏色；「出發」那一欄用的是畫家的色相環上的顏色。

points.en: Which pairs of colors count as complementary depends on the color model you use. With red, yellow, and blue as primaries, the pairs are red and green, yellow and purple, blue and orange. With red, green, and blue, they are red and cyan, green and magenta, blue and yellow.
points.zh: 哪兩個顏色算互補，要看用的是哪一套色彩模型。以紅、黃、藍為原色時，是紅和綠、黃和紫、藍和橙；以紅、綠、藍為原色時，是紅和青、綠和洋紅、藍和黃。

points.en: Mixing shows the same split. Two complementary lights at full strength add up to white. Paints work by absorbing light, so complementary paints mix toward gray or black.
points.zh: 混色的結果也分成兩種。兩種互補的色光都開到最亮，加起來是白光；顏料靠吸收光來顯色，所以互補的顏料混在一起會偏向灰或黑。

points.en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary has both ideas. Its entry for 互補色 speaks of two colored lights that mix to white and gives yellow and blue light as the example. Its entry for 對比色 gives red and green, yellow and purple.
points.zh: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》兩種說法都有。「互補色」一條講的是色光：「任何二種色光等量混合而成白色時，則此二色互為互補色。例如黃色光與藍色光」；「對比色」一條舉的例子則是「紅與綠、黃與紫」。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Wheel · 色相環背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A circle of seven colors, a black dye, an old observation, and a third direction
culture_cards.title_zh: 七個顏色的圓、一種黑色染料、一個很老的觀察，和第三個方向
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learned to arrange colors and to notice how they change each other.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼排列顏色、又怎麼注意到顏色會互相影響的四個小故事。

cards.en: Newton bends the rainbow into a circle
cards.zh: 牛頓把彩虹彎成一個圓
cards.body_en: Isaac Newton's book Opticks, published in 1704, contained the first color wheel. He set the seven colors of the spectrum into a circle, in segments of unequal size that followed the pattern of a musical scale. His circle showed only the colors of the spectrum. Later wheels added the purples that join the red end to the violet end.
cards.body_zh: 牛頓 1704 年出版的《光學》裡有第一個色環。他把光譜的七個顏色排成一個圓，每一格大小不一，照的是音階的規律。他的色環只有光譜上的顏色；後來的色相環才補上把紅端和紫端接起來的那些紫紅色。

cards.body_en: In 1824 the chemist Michel Eugène Chevreul was put in charge of the dye works at the Gobelins factory in Paris, after complaints about its colors. He found some dyes at fault, but the black that people criticized most was first-rate. Cloth dyed with it looked weak and reddish only when deep blues or purples lay around it. He called the effect simultaneous contrast and wrote a book about it in 1839.
cards.body_zh: 1824 年，化學家謝弗勒在外界抱怨顏色有問題之後，接掌巴黎戈布蘭工廠的染坊。他發現有些染料確實不好，但被批評得最兇的黑色其實是上等的；用它染的布，只有在周圍是深藍或深紫的時候，才顯得又淡又偏紅。他把這個效果叫做同時對比，並在 1839 年寫成一本書。

cards.k: About 1,000 Years Ago · 大約一千年前
cards.body_en: The oldest known scientific note on this effect comes from the physicist Ibn al-Haytham in the eleventh century. He described spots of paint that looked almost black on a white background and paler than their true color on a black one. Goethe wrote down the same thing about gray shapes in 1810. People have been surprised by it for a very long time.
cards.body_zh: 目前所知最早寫下這個現象的科學文獻，出自十一世紀的物理學家海什木（Ibn al-Haytham）：他描述顏料的小點放在白色的底上看起來幾乎是黑的，放在黑色的底上又比原來的顏色淡。歌德在 1810 年也對灰色的圖形寫下同樣的觀察。人們為這件事感到驚訝，已經很久很久了。

cards.zh: 孟塞爾多加了兩個方向
cards.body_en: A flat wheel shows hue and nothing else. In the first decade of the twentieth century the American painter Albert Munsell built a system on three properties of color: hue, value (how light), and chroma (how strong). His hue circle has five principal hues: red, yellow, green, blue, and purple. Lesson 3 goes up and down the direction that the wheel leaves out, from light to dark.
cards.body_zh: 一個平面的色相環只能表示色相。二十世紀的頭十年，美國畫家孟塞爾（Albert Munsell）用顏色的三個性質建立了一套系統：色相、明度（多亮）和彩度（多鮮豔）。他的色相環有五個主要色相：紅、黃、綠、藍、紫。第三課會沿著色相環沒有畫出來的那個方向走：從亮到暗。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum does not name the color wheel, complementary colors, or warm and cool colors. These are the closest entries. The links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱的條文沒有點名色相環、互補色或寒暖色。下面是最接近的條目；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 色彩感知、造形與空間的探索。
items.note_en: Noticing that a color changes with its surroundings is part of sensing color.
items.note_zh: 察覺一個顏色會隨周圍改變，是色彩感知的一部分。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Words such as analogous, complementary, warm, and cool let students say what they see.
items.note_zh: 類似色、互補色、暖色、冷色這些詞，讓學生能說出自己看到的。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 藝術語彙、形式原理與視覺美感。
items.note_en: Contrast is one of the ideas students use when they talk about how a picture is put together.
items.note_zh: 討論一張圖怎麼組成時，對比是會用到的觀念之一。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國中）
items.text: 色彩理論、造形表現、符號意涵。
items.note_en: Color wheels and color schemes belong to color theory. The entry does not list them by name.
items.note_zh: 色相環與配色屬於色彩理論，但這一條沒有點名。

myths.myth_en: The opposite of red is green, and that is the only answer.
myths.myth_zh: 紅色的對面就是綠色，只有這一個答案。
myths.fact_en: It depends on the wheel. On the painter's wheel, built on red, yellow, and blue, green is across from red. On the screen wheel, built on red, green, and blue, the color across from red is cyan.
myths.fact_zh: 要看是哪一個色相環。在以紅、黃、藍為基礎的畫家色相環上，紅色對面是綠色；在以紅、綠、藍為基礎的螢幕色相環上，紅色對面是青色。

myths.myth_en: If two patches look different, they must be different colors.
myths.myth_zh: 兩塊顏色看起來不一樣，就一定是不同的顏色。
myths.fact_en: The same gray looks lighter on black and darker on white. The patches are equal. What differs is the background, and the eye judges a color against what is around it.
myths.fact_zh: 同一個灰色，放在黑色上看起來比較淺，放在白色上看起來比較深。兩塊其實一樣，不一樣的是底色；眼睛判斷顏色，是拿它和周圍比較。

myths.myth_en: Science has proved that warm colors excite people and cool colors calm them.
myths.myth_zh: 科學已經證明暖色讓人興奮、冷色讓人平靜。
myths.fact_en: Warm and cool are names artists use for two sides of the wheel. A review of the research on color and feelings says it is too early for firm claims, and one well-known early claim could not be repeated by other researchers.
myths.fact_zh: 「暖」和「冷」是藝術家對色相環兩側的稱呼。一篇整理顏色與心理研究的回顧文章說，現在要下定論還太早；早期一個很有名的說法，後來別的研究者也無法重複出來。

myths.myth_en: There are rules for which colors match, and breaking them is wrong.
myths.myth_zh: 顏色怎麼配有一定的規則，不照規則就是錯。
myths.fact_en: Color schemes are guides that many artists find useful. How pleasing a combination looks also depends on the person, the place, and the culture, so no formula can decide it for everyone.
myths.fact_zh: 配色的方法是很多藝術家覺得好用的參考。一組顏色好不好看，也和看的人、場合與文化有關，所以沒有一條公式能替所有人決定。

tricks_head.en: The color wheel in a sentence

tricks.body_en: Neighbors on the wheel are analogous colors. They look close and quiet together.
tricks.body_zh: 色相環上的鄰居是類似色，放在一起很接近、很安靜。

tricks.body_en: Opposites are complementary colors. Each makes the other stand out.
tricks.body_zh: 對面的顏色是互補色，會互相襯托。

tricks.body_en: Red faces green on the painter's wheel and cyan on the screen wheel.
tricks.body_zh: 紅色在畫家的色相環上對著綠，在螢幕的色相環上對著青。

tricks.title_en: A color changes with its neighbors
tricks.body_en: The same gray looks lighter on black and darker on white.
tricks.body_zh: 同一個灰色，放在黑色上比較淺，放在白色上比較深。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Rest your eyes. Taiwan's Health Promotion Administration advises ten minutes of rest after every thirty minutes of close work, and at least 120 minutes outdoors each day.
safety.zh: 讓眼睛休息。國民健康署建議：用眼每 30 分鐘休息 10 分鐘，每天戶外活動 120 分鐘以上。

safety.en: Carry scissors closed, with the points down, and hand them to someone handle first. Cut away from your other hand.
safety.zh: 拿剪刀走動時要合起來、尖端朝下；遞給別人時握柄朝向對方。剪的時候，另一隻手不要放在刀口前面。

safety.en: Keep food and drinks away from the paint. Do not put paint or brushes in your mouth, and wash your hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 食物和飲料不要放在顏料旁邊。顏料和畫筆不要放進嘴巴；畫完要洗手。

safety.en: Cover the desk before you paint, and let each paper dry flat before you stack it.
safety.zh: 上色之前先把桌面鋪好；每一張紙都平放晾乾之後再疊起來。

materials.en: One sheet of medium gray paper
materials.zh: 一張中等深淺的灰色紙

materials.en: One sheet of black paper and one of white paper
materials.zh: 黑紙和白紙各一張

materials.en: Colored paper in yellow and blue
materials.zh: 黃色和藍色的色紙

materials.en: Scissors, a ruler, and a pencil
materials.zh: 剪刀、尺和鉛筆

steps.en: Cut four squares, three centimeters on each side, from the same sheet of gray paper.
steps.zh: 從同一張灰紙上剪下四個邊長三公分的正方形。

steps.en: Lay one square in the middle of the black paper and one in the middle of the white paper. Put the two papers side by side.
steps.zh: 一塊放在黑紙中央，一塊放在白紙中央，再把兩張紙並排。

steps.en: Ask five classmates which square looks darker. Write down each answer.
steps.zh: 問五位同學：哪一塊看起來比較深？把每個人的答案記下來。

steps.en: Now slide the two squares until they touch. Do they still look different? Write down what you see.
steps.zh: 把兩塊灰色推到互相碰在一起。它們看起來還不一樣嗎？把看到的寫下來。

steps.en: Repeat with the other two squares on yellow and on blue paper. Then compare your paper results with the squares on this page.
steps.zh: 用另外兩塊在黃紙和藍紙上再做一次。最後把紙上的結果和這一頁螢幕上的方塊比一比。

activities.tip_en: Not everyone sees the effect equally strongly, and paper and screens do not behave the same way. Record what people actually say, including anyone who sees no difference.
activities.tip_zh: 不是每個人看到的效果都一樣明顯，紙和螢幕的表現也不相同。請照實記下大家說的，包括說「看不出差別」的人。

materials.en: Three copies of the same simple line drawing, such as a house and two hills
materials.zh: 同一張簡單的線稿三份，例如一間小屋和兩座山丘

materials.en: Colored pencils, crayons, or watercolors with at least twelve colors
materials.zh: 色鉛筆、蠟筆或水彩，至少十二色

materials.en: This page, with the painter's wheel showing
materials.zh: 這一頁，並把色相環切換到畫家的色相環

steps.en: On the wheel, pick a main color. Write down its number and name, and the names of its two neighbors.
steps.zh: 在色相環上選一個主色，寫下它的編號和名稱，以及兩個鄰居的名稱。

steps.en: Color the first copy with those three analogous colors. Find the closest pencils or paints you have.
steps.zh: 用這三個類似色替第一張上色；從手邊的筆或顏料裡找最接近的。

steps.en: Color the second copy with your main color and the color across the wheel from it.
steps.zh: 第二張用主色和它在色相環正對面的顏色上色。

steps.en: Color the third copy with three colors spaced evenly around the wheel.
steps.zh: 第三張用色相環上平均分開的三個顏色上色。

steps.en: Pin up all three. From across the room, which one do you notice first? Hold each copy beside the screen. Where do your colors differ from the model's?
steps.zh: 把三張都貼起來。從教室另一頭看，最先注意到哪一張？再把每一張拿到螢幕旁邊：你的顏色和模型的顏色，哪裡不一樣？

activities.tip_en: Your pencils will not match the screen, and that is expected: the wheel on this page is made of light, and its swatches only stand for the color names. There is no single right answer about which copy looks best. Ask your classmates and count the votes.
activities.tip_zh: 你的筆和螢幕的顏色不會一樣，這是正常的：這一頁的色相環是光做的，色塊只是代表那些顏色的名稱。哪一張最好看，沒有唯一的答案；問問同學，數一數票數。

links_head.en: Where the two wheels come from, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 兩個色相環從哪裡來，以及下一課

links.en: Why Do Paint and Light Mix Differently?
links.zh: 顏料和光，混色為什麼不一樣？
links.note_en: Light adds and paint takes away. That is why there is one wheel for screens and another for paint.
links.note_zh: 光是加，顏料是減。所以螢幕有螢幕的色相環，顏料有顏料的色相環。

links.note_en: Newton made his circle from the colors of the spectrum. That lesson shows where those colors come from.
links.note_zh: 牛頓的色環是用光譜的顏色排成的；那一課講這些顏色是怎麼來的。

links.en: How Does Shading Make a Circle Look Like a Ball?
links.zh: 明暗怎麼把圓形變成球？
links.note_en: Next comes the direction the wheel leaves out: light and dark, and a lamp you can drag around a ball.
links.note_zh: 下一課是色相環沒有畫出來的方向：明與暗，還有一盞可以繞著球拖動的燈。

lessons.title: How Does Shading Make a Circle Look Like a Ball?
lessons.title_zh: 明暗怎麼把圓形變成球？
lessons.blurb_en: Move one lamp around a ball and watch the light side, the dark side, and the shadow follow it. Then take the shading away and see the ball turn back into a flat circle.
lessons.blurb_zh: 拿一盞燈繞著一顆球移動，看亮面、暗面和影子跟著它變；再把明暗拿掉，看球變回一個平面的圓。
lessons.big_idea_en: An outline can only tell you that a shape is a circle. Shading tells you that it is a ball. The surface is lightest where it faces the lamp and grows darker as it turns away, and the shadow falls on the side away from the lamp. Light, shade, and shadow all follow the light source.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 輪廓只能告訴你這個形狀是圓的；明暗才能告訴你它是一顆球。表面朝著燈的地方最亮，越轉離燈就越暗，影子落在背向燈的那一邊。亮面、暗面和影子，全部跟著光源走。

lab.title_en: A Ball, a Table, and One Lamp
lab.title_zh: 一顆球、一張桌子，和一盞燈
lab.how_en: Drag the lamp, or use the two sliders, to move it around the ball and up and down. The labels name the parts of the light and shade. Point at any spot on the ball to read how light it is. Then press Flat circle to take all the shading away, or Pencil steps to sort the grays into a few steps the way you would with a pencil.
lab.how_zh: 拖動那盞燈，或用兩根滑桿，讓它繞著球轉、升高或降低。標籤寫著明暗各部分的名稱；指著球上任何一點，就能讀出那裡有多亮。再按「平面的圓」把明暗全部拿掉，或按「分階」把灰分成幾階，就像用鉛筆畫的那樣。

legend.en: The lamp, which only marks where the light comes from
legend.zh: 燈：只是標出光從哪裡來

legend.en: The dashed line: the direction of the light
The small dot: the spot whose gray is read out on the right
legend.zh: 小圓點：右邊讀出的是這一點的灰

lab.scale_en: The grays are screen values from 0 (black) to 255 (white). L* is a measure of lightness from 0 to 100. The ball and the table are drawn straight from the numbers, with no other lighting added.
lab.scale_zh: 灰色是螢幕的設定值，從 0（黑）到 255（白）。L* 是明度的量，從 0 到 100。球和桌面直接照這些數字畫出來，沒有再加別的光影。

notes.en: The lamp is treated as a light very far away, so only its direction matters. A real lamp close to a ball lights it a little differently, and its shadow spreads out.
notes.zh: 模型把燈當成非常遠的光，所以只看方向。真正的燈離球很近的時候，照出來的樣子會有一點不同，影子也會往外張開。

notes.en: The reflected light under the ball comes from one simple rule. The model does not follow light as it bounces around a real room.
notes.zh: 球底下的反光只用一條簡單的規則算出來；模型沒有真的去追蹤光在房間裡來回反射。

notes.en: The edge of the shadow is drawn with one fixed softness. Real shadow edges are sharper near the object and softer farther away, and softer still when the lamp is large.
notes.zh: 影子的邊緣用固定的柔和程度來畫。真正的影子，靠近物體的地方比較清楚，越遠越模糊；燈越大，邊緣也越柔和。

notes.en: The ball is plain gray and a little shiny. Real things have color and texture, and a matte ball has no bright highlight.
notes.zh: 這顆球是單純的灰色，表面有一點光澤。真實的東西有顏色和質感；表面不反光的球，就沒有明顯的亮點。

lab.note_end_en: So set up a real ball and a real lamp and compare. Classroom Activity 1 shows how.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請拿真的球和真的燈來比一比；做法在課堂活動一。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn for this lesson. The shading formula is in the shared color engine and is covered by automatic tests. · 模型為本課自行繪製；明暗的公式放在共用的顏色引擎裡，並有自動測試。

paras: Draw a circle on a sheet of paper. It could be a coin, a plate, or a hole. Nothing in the outline tells you which. Now make one side of the circle light and let it grow darker little by little toward the other side, and add a dark patch on the ground beside it. Suddenly the circle is a ball. The outline did not change. What you added is shading, and shading is how a flat drawing shows that a thing is round.

Shading copies what light does. Put a ball on a table and switch on one lamp. The part of the ball that faces the lamp gets the most light. As the surface curves away, the same light is spread over more of it, so it looks darker. Where the surface turns its back on the lamp, no direct light arrives at all. Every gray on the ball depends on one thing: how squarely that spot faces the light.

Artists have names for the parts. The highlight is the brightest spot, where a shiny surface sends the lamp's light straight to your eye. The light side shades into the halftone, the middle grays. Then comes the core shadow, a soft dark band that begins where the direct light ends. Beyond it the shadow side is often a little lighter again. That is reflected light, which bounces up from the table onto the ball.

The ball also blocks light from reaching the table, and that makes a cast shadow. A cast shadow always points away from the lamp. Raise the lamp and the shadow gets shorter. Lower the lamp and it stretches out, the way your own shadow does late in the afternoon. A small lamp gives a shadow with a crisp edge. The wider the light source, the more blurred the shadow becomes.

You do not need hundreds of grays to draw a ball. How light or dark a color is, is called its value, and a value scale is a row of even steps from white to black. In the Munsell system, value runs from 0 for black to 10 for white. In 1907 the teacher Denman Ross described a scale of nine values. With only five steps of pencil gray, placed in the right places, a circle already looks round.

Painters have used light and shade this way for centuries. The Italian word chiaroscuro means light-dark, and it describes clear contrasts of tone that suggest the volume of the things in a painting. Leonardo da Vinci and Caravaggio are famous for it. You can see the same thing in the night sky. The Sun always lights half of the Moon, like one lamp shining on one ball, and what we call the phases are our changing view of that sunlit half.
paras_zh: 在紙上畫一個圓。它可能是一枚硬幣、一個盤子，或是一個洞；光看輪廓，分不出是哪一個。現在讓圓的一邊亮，往另一邊一點一點變暗，再在旁邊的地面上加一塊暗暗的形狀。忽然之間，圓變成了一顆球。輪廓並沒有改變，你加上去的是明暗；平面的圖畫，就是靠明暗來表現一樣東西是圓鼓鼓的。
明暗是照著光的行為畫出來的。把一顆球放在桌上，打開一盞燈。球面朝著燈的部分，得到的光最多。表面越彎離燈，同樣多的光要攤在更大的面積上，所以看起來比較暗。到了背對燈的地方，就完全沒有直接照到的光了。球上每一處的灰，只看一件事：那一點有多正對著光。
藝術家替這幾個部分取了名字。亮點是最亮的一小塊，有光澤的表面在那裡把燈光直接反射到你的眼睛。亮面慢慢過渡到半色調，也就是中間的灰。再過去是最暗的那一圈（英文叫 core shadow），一道柔和的暗帶，從直接的光結束的地方開始。過了這一圈，暗面常常又稍微亮一點，那是反光：光從桌面彈上來，照到球上。
球也擋住了照向桌面的光，於是桌上有了投影，也就是影子。影子永遠指向燈的反方向。把燈舉高，影子變短；把燈放低，影子拉長，就像傍晚時你自己的影子。小小的燈照出邊緣清楚的影子；光源越寬，影子就越模糊。
畫一顆球，不需要幾百種灰。一個顏色有多亮或多暗，叫做它的明度；明度階是從白到黑、一階一階間隔相等的一排灰。在孟塞爾系統裡，明度從 0（黑）到 10（白）。1907 年，美術教師羅斯（Denman Ross）描述過一套九階的明度。其實只要五階的鉛筆灰，放在對的位置，一個圓看起來就已經是圓鼓鼓的了。
幾百年來，畫家一直這樣運用明與暗。義大利文 chiaroscuro 的意思是「明—暗」，指的是用清楚的明暗對比來表現畫中物體的體積；達文西和卡拉瓦喬都以此聞名。同樣的事，在夜空中也看得到：太陽永遠照亮月球的一半，就像一盞燈照著一顆球；我們說的月相，就是從地球上看到的那一半亮面一直在改變。
questions: A drawn circle and a drawn ball have the same outline. What makes one of them look round?
You see a ball whose shadow is very long and points to the right. Where is the lamp?
Why is the shadow side of a ball on a white table usually not completely black?
answers: Shading. The ball is lightest where it faces the light and gets darker as its surface turns away, and it has a cast shadow beside it. The flat circle is one even gray.
On the left, and low. A cast shadow points away from the lamp, and a low lamp makes a long shadow.
Light bounces off the table and other things nearby and reaches the shadow side. Artists call this reflected light.

vocab.ex: Careful shading makes the circle look like a ball.
vocab.exzh: 仔細畫出明暗，圓看起來就像一顆球。

vocab.ex: The highlight is the brightest spot on the ball.
vocab.exzh: 亮點是球上最亮的地方。

vocab.ex: The ball's shadow falls on the side away from the lamp.
vocab.exzh: 球的影子落在背向燈的那一邊。

vocab.ex: A low lamp casts a long shadow.
vocab.exzh: 燈放得低，投出來的影子就長。

vocab.ex: The white table reflects light onto the dark side of the ball.
vocab.exzh: 白色的桌面把光反射到球的暗面。

vocab.ex: Yellow has a light value, and dark blue has a dark one.
vocab.exzh: 黃色的明度高，深藍色的明度低。

vocab.ex: The outline of a ball is only a circle.
vocab.exzh: 球的輪廓只是一個圓。

vocab.ex: The surface gets darker as it turns away from the light.
vocab.exzh: 表面越轉離光，就越暗。

quiz.q: Which part of a ball is lightest?
options: The part that faces the lamp
The part that touches the table
The part farthest from the lamp
The edge of the cast shadow

quiz.q: Which way does a cast shadow point?
What happens to the shadow on the table when the lamp is lowered?
What is reflected light?
options: The brightest spot on the ball
Light that bounces from nearby surfaces onto the shadow side
Light that passes through the ball

quiz.q: What does “value” mean in art?
options: How light or dark a color is

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: First the ball is drawn with no shading at all: a flat gray circle. Then the shading comes back, and the circle swells into a ball.
parts.text_zh: 先把球畫成完全沒有明暗的樣子：一個平面的灰色圓。接著明暗回來，圓就鼓成了一顆球。

parts.text_en: The lamp moves from the left side to the right. The light side, the dark band, and the shadow on the table all swing around with it.
parts.text_zh: 燈從左邊移到右邊。亮面、最暗的那一圈和桌上的影子，全部跟著它轉。

parts.text_en: With the lamp high, the shadow is a short patch under the ball. As the lamp comes down, the shadow stretches far across the table.
parts.text_zh: 燈很高的時候，影子是球底下短短的一塊；燈降下來，影子就在桌面上拉得很長。

parts.text_en: The same light is sorted into seven steps of gray, then five, then three. Even with three, you still read the shape as a ball.
parts.text_zh: 同樣的光，分成七階的灰，再變成五階、三階。就算只有三階，你還是看得出那是一顆球。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Where must the lamp be for the shadow to hide completely behind the ball? Where is it when the ball looks flattest?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。燈要放在哪裡，影子才會完全躲到球的後面？球看起來最扁平的時候，燈又在哪裡？

lamp.lead_en: Six pictures of a ball on a table. In each one, work out where the light comes from. Find the lightest part of the ball first, then check which way the shadow points. Every choice has an arrow and words. The game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
lamp.lead_zh: 六張桌上一顆球的圖。每一張都要判斷光從哪裡來：先找球上最亮的地方，再看影子指向哪一邊。每個選項都有箭頭和文字。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。
lamp.note_en: The pictures are drawn with the same formula as the model above, seen from straight in front.
lamp.note_zh: 這些圖用的是和上面模型同一條公式，從正前方看。

sort.lead_en: Five gray squares are out of order. Click one square and then another to trade their places, until the lightest is on the left and the darkest on the right. Then press Check. There are three rounds, and in each round the grays are closer together.
sort.lead_zh: 五塊灰色的方塊順序亂了。點一塊、再點另一塊，兩塊就會交換位置；排到最亮的在左邊、最暗的在右邊，再按「對答案」。一共三回合，每一回合的灰色彼此更接近。
sort.note_en: After you finish a round, each square shows its L*, a number for lightness from 0 (black) to 100 (white). Remember Lesson 2: a gray can look lighter or darker depending on what is beside it, so the last round is harder than it sounds.
sort.note_zh: 每完成一回合，方塊下面會顯示 L*：明度的數字，從 0（黑）到 100（白）。別忘了第二課：一個灰看起來比較亮或比較暗，和它旁邊是什麼有關，所以最後一回合比聽起來難。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Shadows · 明暗背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A word for light-dark, a smoky edge, a ball in the sky, and nine grays
culture_cards.title_zh: 「明—暗」這個詞、煙霧一樣的邊緣、天上的一顆球，和九階灰
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people have used and studied light and shade.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼運用、怎麼研究明與暗的四個小故事。

cards.k: A Word from Italy · 來自義大利的詞
cards.body_en: Chiaroscuro is an Italian term that literally means light-dark. The National Gallery in London uses it for clear contrasts of tone that suggest the volume and modeling of the things in a painting, and names Leonardo da Vinci and Caravaggio as artists famed for it. In Caravaggio's late paintings, faces and hands are lit against a setting that is mostly dark. That stronger kind has its own name, tenebrism.
cards.body_zh: chiaroscuro 是義大利文，字面的意思是「明—暗」。倫敦國家美術館用這個詞指清楚的明暗對比，用來表現畫中物體的體積與立體感，並舉達文西和卡拉瓦喬為以此聞名的畫家。卡拉瓦喬晚期的畫裡，臉和手被照亮，周圍大部分是暗的；這種更強烈的做法另有一個名稱，叫暗色調主義（tenebrism）。

cards.body_en: Look at the edge of the ball in the model. There is no line around it. One gray simply meets another. Leonardo da Vinci advised painting without lines. The soft, smoky way he blurred his contours is called sfumato: figures emerge from a dark background through gradual changes of tone, with no harsh outlines.
cards.body_zh: 看看模型裡那顆球的邊緣：它周圍並沒有一條線，只是一種灰碰到另一種灰。達文西主張畫畫「不用線條」。他把輪廓弄得柔和、像煙霧一樣的畫法，叫做暈塗法（sfumato）：人物靠著一點一點變化的明暗，從暗暗的背景裡浮現出來，沒有生硬的輪廓線。

cards.en: The Moon is a ball lit by one lamp
cards.zh: 月球就是一盞燈照著的一顆球
cards.body_en: The Sun always lights half of the Moon while the other half stays dark. The line between lunar day and night is called the terminator, and long shadows there make craters and mountains easy to see. The dark part of a crescent Moon is sometimes faintly visible too. NASA calls that earthshine: sunlight that reflects off the Earth onto the Moon. It is the same reflected light you see under the ball.
cards.body_zh: 太陽永遠照亮月球的一半，另一半是暗的。月面上白天和黑夜的分界線叫做明暗界線（terminator）；那裡的影子很長，坑洞和山脈特別容易看清楚。彎彎的月亮暗的那一部分，有時候也隱約看得見。NASA 把它叫做地照（earthshine）：陽光先從地球反射到月球上。這和你在球底下看到的反光，是同一回事。

cards.body_en: How many steps should a value scale have? In A Theory of Pure Design, published in 1907, the American teacher Denman Ross set out a scale of nine neutral values, with white the highest and black the lowest. Albert Munsell's system, from the same years, numbers value from 0 for black to 10 for white. The number of steps is a choice. Seeing the steps clearly is the skill.
cards.body_zh: 明度階應該分成幾階？美國美術教師羅斯在 1907 年出版的《A Theory of Pure Design》裡，列出一套九階的中性明度：白最高、黑最低。同一個年代，孟塞爾的系統把明度從 0（黑）編到 10（白）。分幾階是一種選擇；能把每一階看清楚，才是真正要練的功夫。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum does not use the words for light and shade or for shadow. These are the closest entries, together with two from science. The links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱的條文沒有出現「明暗」「光影」或「陰影」。下面是最接近的條目，另外加上自然科學的兩條；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 色彩感知、造形與空間的探索。
items.note_en: Shading is one way a flat drawing explores form and space.
items.note_zh: 明暗是平面的圖探索造形與空間的一種方法。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.note_en: Building up steps of gray with a pencil is a basic technique.
items.note_zh: 用鉛筆一階一階疊出灰，是一種基本技法。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國中）
items.text: 平面、立體及複合媒材的表現技法。
items.note_en: Showing a solid form on a flat surface is the subject of this lesson.
items.note_zh: 在平面上表現立體，正是這一課的主題。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 光線以直線前進，反射時有一定的方向。
items.note_en: Light travels in straight lines, which is why a shadow points away from the lamp.
items.note_zh: 光沿直線前進，所以影子會指向燈的反方向。

items.text: 由針孔成像、影子實驗驗證與說明光的直進性。
items.note_en: The shadow experiments in the classroom activities fit here.
items.note_zh: 課堂活動裡的影子實驗對得上這一條。

myths.myth_en: To make a drawing look real, you need a strong, dark outline.
myths.myth_zh: 要畫得像真的，輪廓線要畫得又黑又清楚。
myths.fact_en: An outline shows only the shape of the edge. A ball looks round because of its shading and its cast shadow. Real objects have no line around them at all.
myths.fact_zh: 輪廓線只表現邊緣的形狀。球看起來圓鼓鼓的，靠的是明暗和投影。真實的物體周圍，其實根本沒有一條線。

myths.myth_en: The darkest part of a ball is the part farthest from the lamp.
myths.myth_zh: 球上最暗的地方，就是離燈最遠的地方。
myths.fact_en: The darkest part is often a band just past the edge of the direct light, called the core shadow. Farther around, reflected light from the table makes the surface a little lighter again.
myths.fact_zh: 最暗的地方，往往是直接的光剛結束的那一圈（core shadow）。再往後，桌面彈上來的反光又讓表面稍微亮了一點。

myths.fact_en: A shadow is a place that direct light does not reach. Light reflected from other surfaces usually still gets in, and when the light source is wide, the edge of the shadow is blurred.
myths.fact_zh: 影子是直接的光照不到的地方。別的表面反射過來的光通常還是照得進去；光源比較寬的時候，影子的邊緣也是模糊的。

myths.myth_en: Pencil lead is made of lead.
myths.fact_en: Pencil lead is not lead. Most pencil cores are made of graphite powder mixed with clay. That is still no reason to put a pencil in your mouth.
myths.fact_zh: 鉛筆的「鉛」不是鉛。大多數鉛筆芯是石墨粉加黏土做成的。不過這不代表可以把鉛筆放進嘴巴。

tricks_head.en: Light and shade in a sentence

tricks.body_en: A surface is lightest where it faces the lamp and darker as it turns away.
tricks.body_zh: 表面朝著燈的地方最亮，越轉離燈越暗。

tricks.body_en: The cast shadow always lies on the side away from the lamp.
tricks.body_zh: 投影永遠落在背向燈的那一邊。

tricks.body_en: High lamp, short shadow. Think of noon and late afternoon.
tricks.body_zh: 燈越高，影子越短。想想正午和傍晚。

tricks.body_en: Look for reflected light on the shadow side before you fill it in black.
tricks.body_zh: 把暗面塗黑之前，先找找裡面的反光。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前
safety_head.en: Lamps, pencils, and a dark room

safety.en: Do not look straight into the lamp, and do not point it at anyone's eyes. Look at the ball and the shadow.
safety.zh: 不要直視燈，也不要拿燈照別人的眼睛。看球和影子就好。

safety.en: A lamp bulb can get hot. Let an adult move it, or wait until it has cooled. Keep the cord out of the way so nobody trips.
safety.zh: 燈泡可能會燙。請大人移動它，或等它涼了再碰。電線收好，免得有人絆倒。

safety.en: Pencil lead is graphite, not lead, but pencils still do not belong in your mouth. Wash the graphite off your hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 鉛筆芯是石墨，不是鉛，但鉛筆還是不該放進嘴巴。畫完把手上的石墨洗掉。

safety.en: Before the room goes dark, clear the floor. Rest your eyes too: ten minutes after every thirty minutes of close work.
safety.zh: 關燈之前先把地板清空。也要讓眼睛休息：用眼每 30 分鐘休息 10 分鐘。

activities.title_en: A Real Ball and a Real Lamp

materials.en: A plain, light-colored ball, such as a table tennis ball or a foam ball
materials.zh: 一顆素色、淺色的球，例如桌球或保麗龍球

materials.en: A desk lamp or a flashlight, in a room you can make dim
materials.zh: 一盞檯燈或一支手電筒，以及一間可以弄暗的教室

materials.en: A sheet of white paper and a sheet of black paper to stand the ball on
materials.zh: 白紙和黑紙各一張，用來墊在球下面

materials.en: This page, with the model set to Ball
materials.zh: 這一頁，模型設在「球」

steps.en: Put the ball on the white paper. Dim the room and shine the lamp on the ball from the upper left.
steps.zh: 把球放在白紙上。把教室弄暗，從左上方用燈照球。

steps.en: Find the lightest spot, the darkest band, and the cast shadow. Point to each one and say its name.
steps.zh: 找出最亮的地方、最暗的那一圈和投影。一個一個指出來，說出名稱。

steps.en: Set the lamp in the model to about the same place. What is the same on the screen and on your desk? What is different?
steps.zh: 把模型裡的燈調到差不多的位置。螢幕上和桌上，哪些一樣？哪些不一樣？

steps.en: Look at the shadow side near the table. Now slide the black paper under the ball in place of the white. Does that part get darker?
steps.zh: 看球的暗面靠近桌面的地方。把白紙換成黑紙墊在球下面，那個地方有沒有變暗？

steps.en: Move the lamp lower, then higher. Measure the shadow each time with a ruler and write the numbers down.
steps.zh: 把燈放低，再舉高。每一次都用尺量影子的長度，把數字記下來。

activities.tip_en: Your shadow will not match the model exactly. The model treats the lamp as very far away, and a real lamp is close and has some width, so its shadow spreads and its edge is soft. A matte ball may have no bright highlight at all. Finding these differences is the point.
activities.tip_zh: 你的影子不會和模型一模一樣。模型把燈當成非常遠，真的燈很近、又有寬度，所以影子會張開、邊緣是柔和的；表面不反光的球，可能根本沒有明顯的亮點。找出這些差別，正是這個活動的目的。

materials.en: A soft pencil, such as a 2B, and white drawing paper
materials.zh: 一支軟的鉛筆（例如 2B）和白色的圖畫紙

materials.en: An eraser and a ruler
materials.zh: 橡皮擦和尺

materials.en: The ball and lamp from Activity 1, or the model set to Pencil steps with 5 steps
materials.zh: 活動一的球和燈，或把模型設在「分階」、五階

steps.en: Draw a row of five boxes. Leave the first one white and make the last one as dark as your pencil will go.
steps.zh: 畫一排五個格子。第一格留白，最後一格塗到這支鉛筆能塗的最黑。

steps.en: Fill the three boxes between them so that each step is the same size. This is your value scale.
steps.zh: 把中間三格塗上灰，讓每一階的差距一樣大。這就是你的明度階。

steps.en: Draw a light circle. Mark where the light comes from with a small arrow outside it.
steps.zh: 輕輕畫一個圓，在圓的外面用小箭頭標出光從哪裡來。

steps.en: Shade the ball using only your five grays: the lightest toward the arrow, the darkest in a band on the far side, and a slightly lighter gray below that band.
steps.zh: 只用你的五階灰替球畫上明暗：最亮的朝著箭頭，最暗的在另一側畫成一圈，那一圈下面再用稍微亮一點的灰。

steps.en: Add the cast shadow on the side away from the arrow. Hold your drawing beside the screen and compare.
steps.zh: 在背向箭頭的那一邊畫上投影。把你的畫拿到螢幕旁邊比一比。

activities.tip_en: Squint at the ball until the small details blur. Squinting makes the big areas of light and dark easier to sort. If your drawing looks flat, the usual reason is that the darkest gray is not dark enough.
activities.tip_zh: 瞇起眼睛看球，直到小細節變模糊；這樣比較容易分出大塊的亮和暗。如果畫出來扁扁的，最常見的原因是最暗的那一階不夠暗。

links_head.en: The same ball in the sky, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 天上的那一顆球，以及下一課

links.en: Why Does the Moon Change Shape?
links.note_en: One lamp, one ball, and a viewer who moves around them. The phases of the Moon are this lesson at full size.
links.note_zh: 一盞燈、一顆球，加上一個繞著它們移動的觀看者。月相就是把這一課放大到真實的尺寸。

links.note_en: The same gray looks lighter on black and darker on white. Keep that in mind when you judge the grays on a ball.
links.note_zh: 同一個灰，放在黑色上比較亮，放在白色上比較暗。判斷球上的灰時，別忘了這件事。

lessons.title: What Can a Line Say?
lessons.blurb_en: Watch one line drawn five ways: light, heavy, fast, shaky, and thick to thin. Then draw on the pad with a mouse, a finger, or a pen, and read what your own line shows about how you made it.
lessons.blurb_zh: 看同一條線用五種方式畫出來：輕、重、快、抖動、由粗到細。再用滑鼠、手指或觸控筆在畫板上畫，讀讀你自己的線透露了哪些畫法。
lessons.big_idea_en: A line is the path of a moving point, and it keeps a record of that movement. Its width shows how hard the tool was pressed. Its edge shows how steady the hand was. Its direction leads the eye. So a line does more than mark the edge of a shape. It also shows how it was made.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 線是一個點移動時走過的路，而且把這段移動記錄了下來。線的粗細看得出下筆多重，邊緣看得出手穩不穩，方向則帶著眼睛走。所以線不只是標出形狀的邊緣，也讓人看出它是怎麼畫出來的。

lab.title_en: One Line, Five Ways, and a Drawing Pad
lab.title_zh: 同一條線的五種畫法，和一塊畫板
lab.how_en: On the left, choose one of five ways to draw the same wavy line and watch it drawn at its real speed. The numbers under it give its length, time, speed, and width. On the right is a drawing pad. Draw with a mouse, a finger, or a pen. A pale tree is there to trace if you like. After each stroke, the page tells you in words how long, how fast, and how wide it was.
lab.how_zh: 左邊可以從五種畫法裡選一種，看同一條波浪線照它真實的速度畫出來；下面的數字是它的長度、時間、速度和粗細。右邊是一塊畫板，用滑鼠、手指或觸控筆都能畫；上面有一棵淡淡的樹，可以照著描。每畫完一筆，頁面會用文字告訴你這一筆多長、多快、多粗。

notes.en: With a mouse or a finger, the pad cannot feel how hard you press. The brush on this page uses speed in its place: a slow stroke is drawn thick and a fast one thin. A pen that senses pressure sets the width by pressure.
notes.zh: 用滑鼠或手指畫的時候，畫板感覺不到你壓得多重。這一頁的毛筆改用速度代替：畫得慢就畫粗，畫得快就畫細。會感應壓力的觸控筆，則是用壓力決定粗細。

notes.en: The gaps in a very fast stroke come from a rule we wrote for this page. With a real brush, such gaps depend on how much ink the brush holds, on the paper, and on the speed together.
notes.zh: 很快的那一筆上面的空隙，是我們替這一頁寫的規則。真的毛筆會不會出現這種空隙，要同時看筆上有多少墨、紙的性質，還有速度。

notes.en: The ink here is one flat black. A real pencil, brush, or crayon also changes in darkness and texture along the line.
notes.zh: 這裡的墨是均勻的一種黑。真的鉛筆、毛筆或蠟筆，線上的深淺和質感也會跟著變。

notes.en: Length, speed, and width are in the pad's own units: the pad is 800 units wide. They are not centimeters.
notes.zh: 長度、速度和粗細用的是畫板自己的單位（畫板寬 800），不是公分。

lab.note_end_en: So try the same five lines with a real pencil and a real brush. Classroom Activity 1 shows how.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請拿真的鉛筆和毛筆，把這五種線畫畫看；做法在課堂活動一。

paras: About 73,000 years ago, someone picked up a piece of ochre and drew a pattern of crossing lines on a stone. A small flake of that stone was found in a cave in South Africa, and it is the oldest drawing we know of. Nobody can say what the lines meant. But the person who drew them did what every child with a crayon still does: pressed a point against a surface and moved it.

That is all a line is. The Getty Museum's teaching pages describe a line as a path made by a point moving in space. A line can change in width, in direction, and in length, and lines often mark the edges of things. A line that follows the outer edge of a shape is called an outline. Lines that travel along the edges and surfaces of an object, so that it looks solid, are called contour lines.

A line also records how it was made. Press harder and the line gets thicker and darker. Hold your hand steady and the edge is clean, and let it tremble and the edge turns rough. Artists call these qualities, thick or thin, hard or soft, dark or light, the line quality. In Chinese painting there is a way of working called baimiao, which uses lines alone, with no color. A skilled painter can show weight, movement, and texture through nothing but the thickness, firmness, and spacing of the lines.

Direction matters too. The Getty pages say that horizontal lines suggest rest, because things that lie flat on the ground are at rest. Vertical lines often give a sense of height. Diagonal lines can give a feeling of movement, because a thing that leans looks as if it might fall. Notice the careful words: suggest, often, can. These are habits of seeing that artists use. They are not rules that every picture must follow.

Lines can do two more jobs. They can close up to make shapes. Geometric shapes are the ones with names from math class, such as squares, triangles, and circles. Organic shapes are irregular, like leaves, clouds, and puddles. Lines can also make shading. Many thin parallel lines set close together look like a gray tone from a distance. This is called hatching, and when a second set of lines crosses the first, it is cross-hatching. That is one way to draw the light and shade from Lesson 3.

In 1925 the painter Paul Klee opened a small book for his students with these words: an active line on a walk, moving freely, without goal. People often shorten this to taking a line for a walk. It is a good way to begin. Put your pencil down, let it travel, and then look at what the line shows. Was it fast or slow? Heavy or light? Sure or unsure? Your line has already said something about you.
paras_zh: 大約七萬三千年前，有人拿起一塊赭石，在石頭上畫了交叉的線條。這塊石頭的一小片，後來在南非的一個洞穴裡被發現，是目前所知最古老的一幅畫。沒有人說得出那些線條的意思。不過畫的人做的事，和今天每個拿著蠟筆的孩子一樣：把一個點壓在一個表面上，然後移動它。
線就是這麼一回事。蓋蒂博物館的教學資料說，線是一個點在空間中移動所形成的路徑；線的粗細、方向和長短都可以改變，而且線常常標出東西的邊緣。沿著一個形狀外緣走的線，叫做外框線（outline）；沿著物體的邊緣和表面走、讓它看起來有立體感的線，叫做輪廓線（contour line）。
線也記錄了它是怎麼畫出來的。壓得重，線就比較粗、比較黑。手很穩，邊緣就乾淨；手一抖，邊緣就毛毛的。粗或細、硬或軟、深或淺，這些特質合起來，藝術家稱為線的品質（line quality）。國畫裡有一種畫法叫白描，只用線條、不上顏色。功夫純熟的畫家，光靠線條的粗細、剛柔和疏密，就能表現出重量、動態和質感。
方向也有關係。蓋蒂的資料說，水平線讓人聯想到休息，因為平躺在地上的東西是靜止的；垂直線常常給人高的感覺；斜線則可以帶來動的感覺，因為傾斜的東西看起來好像快要倒下。請注意這些小心的用詞：「聯想到」「常常」「可以」。這些是藝術家運用的觀看習慣，不是每一張圖都必須遵守的規則。
線還能做另外兩件事。線可以圍起來變成形狀：幾何形是數學課裡有名字的那些，例如正方形、三角形和圓形；有機形（自然的形狀）則是不規則的，像葉子、雲和水窪。線也可以畫出明暗：許多細細的平行線排得很密，從遠處看就像一片灰色。這叫做細線法（hatching）；再加上另一組線和它交叉，就是交叉線法（cross-hatching）。這是畫出第三課那種明暗的一種方法。
1925 年，畫家保羅・克利替學生寫了一本小書，開頭是這樣的：一條主動的線在散步，自由地移動，沒有目的地。大家常把這句話簡化成「帶一條線去散步」。這是很好的起點。把鉛筆放到紙上，讓它走，然後看看這條線透露了什麼：快還是慢？重還是輕？篤定還是猶豫？你的線已經說出了一些關於你的事。
questions: Two lines follow exactly the same path, but one is thick and the other is thin. What was different when they were drawn?
The Getty pages say horizontal lines “suggest” rest. Why is “suggest” a better word here than “mean”?
How can lines alone make part of a drawing look gray?
answers: The pressure. The thick line was made by pressing harder, or with a wider tool. The path can be the same while the line quality is different.
Because it is a habit of seeing and not a rule. Many people connect flat lines with things at rest, but a picture can use horizontal lines in other ways, and viewers do not all react alike.
By hatching. Many thin parallel lines set close together look like a gray tone from a distance, and crossing them with more lines makes the tone darker.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The same path is drawn twice at about the same speed. Only the pressure changes, and the line goes from thin to wide.
parts.text_zh: 同一條路徑，用差不多的速度畫兩次，只有力道不同；線就從細變成寬。

parts.text_en: The whole line is drawn in less than half a second. In this model a stroke that fast leaves gaps. Watch it twice.
parts.text_zh: 整條線不到半秒就畫完了。在這個模型裡，這麼快的一筆會留下空隙。看兩次。

parts.text_en: The line starts with heavy pressure and the tool lifts as it goes. You can tell which end was drawn first.
parts.text_zh: 起筆壓得重，一邊走一邊把筆提起來。看得出哪一頭是先畫的。

parts.text_en: First a steady line, then the same line from a hand that trembles. The path is the same and the edge is different.
parts.text_zh: 先是一條穩穩的線，再來是手在抖的時候畫的同一條線。走的路一樣，邊緣卻不同。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then draw on the pad. Can you draw one line that is thick at the start and thin at the end? Can you draw the tree twice so that it looks calm the first time and windy the second?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後到畫板上畫。你能畫出一條起頭粗、結尾細的線嗎？同一棵樹畫兩次，能不能讓第一次看起來很平靜，第二次像被風吹著？

how.lead_en: Six ink lines. For each one, decide whether it was drawn fast or slowly, and with a heavy or a light touch. Width tells you about pressure. Gaps tell you about speed. After you answer, you can watch the line being drawn at its real speed.
how.lead_zh: 六條墨線。每一條都要判斷：畫得快還是慢？下筆重還是輕？粗細看的是力道，空隙看的是速度。答完之後，可以看這條線用真實的速度重畫一次。
how.note_en: The link between gaps and speed is a rule of this page's brush. With a real brush, the amount of ink and the paper matter as well.
how.note_zh: 「有空隙就是畫得快」是這一頁的毛筆的規則。真的毛筆，還要看筆上有多少墨、用的是什麼紙。

shape.lead_en: A line that closes up makes a shape. Eight dark shapes appear one at a time. Decide whether each is geometric, like the named shapes of math class, or organic, with the irregular curves often found in nature. Each shape has its name under it.
shape.lead_zh: 一條線圍起來，就成了形狀。八個深色的形狀會一個一個出現；判斷每一個是幾何形（像數學課裡有名字的形狀），還是有機形（像自然界裡常見的不規則曲線）。每個形狀下面都寫著名稱。
shape.note_en: The two groups are not perfectly separate. The Getty pages point out that many natural forms have geometric shapes too, and that things people make can imitate organic forms.
shape.note_zh: 這兩類並不是截然分開的。蓋蒂的資料也指出：許多自然的形體同樣帶有幾何的形狀，而人做的東西也可以模仿有機形。
