cards.k: About 73,000 Years Ago · 大約七萬三千年前
cards.en: The oldest drawing we know of
cards.body_en: In 2018 researchers reported a cross-hatched pattern drawn with an ochre crayon on a flake of stone. It came from layers about 73,000 years old in Blombos Cave, South Africa. Drawings that show things or patterns were known before this find only from the last 40,000 years. The stone carries a few crossing lines and no picture of anything. Lines came first.
cards.body_zh: 2018 年，研究者發表了一件用赭石「蠟筆」畫在石片上的交叉線圖案，出自南非布隆伯斯洞穴大約七萬三千年前的地層。在這之前，已知的繪畫（不論畫的是東西還是圖案）都只有四萬年以內的。這片石頭上只有幾條交叉的線，沒有畫出任何東西。最先出現的，是線。

cards.body_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary defines baimiao as a way of painting that draws things with lines alone and adds no color, used mostly for figures and flowers. An education encyclopedia adds that a skilled painter can show solid form, movement, and texture through the thickness, firmness, curve, and spacing of the lines. Chinese painting and calligraphy also share the same tools: brush and ink.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典對「白描」的解釋是：「一種畫法。僅用線條勾描物象，而不著以顏色，多用於人物和花卉的繪畫上。」《教育大辭書》補充：純熟的白描技法，可以藉線條的粗細、剛柔、曲直、疏密等，表現形體的立體感、動態感和質感。國畫和書法用的也是同樣的工具：筆和墨。

cards.body_en: Sometimes a brushstroke has streaks where no ink reached the paper. The Ministry of Education dictionary describes a style of writing named for this look, flying white: strokes with empty, inkless places, as if written with a dry brush. A legend says the Han-dynasty scholar Cai Yong got the idea from watching workmen write with a whitewash broom. The gaps in this page's fast line imitate that look.
cards.body_zh: 有時候一筆畫裡會有幾絲沒沾到墨的空白。教育部辭典記載了一種以此得名的書體「飛白書」：「筆畫中有空白無墨之處，絲絲露白，有如枯筆寫成的模樣。」相傳東漢的蔡邕看見工匠用刷粉的帚寫字，而得到啟發。這一頁那條「很快的線」上的空隙，模仿的就是這種樣子。

cards.body_en: Paul Klee taught at the Bauhaus school in Germany. His Pedagogical Sketchbook, published in 1925, begins: “An active line on a walk, moving freely, without goal. A walk for a walk's sake.” The mover, he wrote, is a point that shifts its position forward. The well-known sayings about taking a line for a walk are shortened versions of this opening.
cards.body_zh: 保羅・克利曾在德國的包浩斯學校教書。他 1925 年出版的《教學筆記》（Pedagogical Sketchbook）這樣開頭：「一條主動的線在散步，自由地移動，沒有目的地。為散步而散步。」他寫道，推動這條線的，是一個不斷往前移動的點。大家熟悉的「帶一條線去散步」，是這段開頭的簡化說法。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum names points, lines, and planes directly for grades 3 and 4. The other entries are the closest ones, and their links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱在國小三、四年級直接點名了「點線面」。其他幾條是最接近的條目；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 點線面創作體驗、平面與立體創作、聯想創作。
items.note_en: This lesson is about the line, from the point that moves to the shape a line closes.
items.note_zh: 這一課講的就是線：從一個移動的點，到線圍成的面。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.note_en: Pencil, marker, and brush each make a different line, and hatching is a technique.
items.note_zh: 鉛筆、粗筆和毛筆各畫出不同的線；細線法是一種技法。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、生活之美、視覺聯想。
items.note_en: Line is one of the visual elements, and reading a line's speed and weight is a kind of visual association.
items.note_zh: 線是視覺元素之一；從一條線讀出快慢與輕重，是一種視覺聯想。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Words such as outline, contour, and hatching let students say what they see.
items.note_zh: 外框線、輪廓線、細線法這些詞，讓學生能說出自己看到的。

myths.myth_en: A line only shows where the edge of a thing is.
myths.myth_zh: 線只是用來標出東西的邊緣。
myths.fact_en: A line also shows how it was made. Its width, its edge, and its gaps record the pressure, the steadiness, and the speed of the hand, and close-set lines can even make shading.
myths.fact_zh: 線也讓人看出它是怎麼畫的：粗細、邊緣和空隙，記錄了下筆的力道、手穩不穩和速度；排得很密的線甚至可以畫出明暗。

myths.myth_en: Horizontal lines always feel calm and diagonal lines always feel exciting.
myths.myth_zh: 水平線一定讓人平靜，斜線一定讓人興奮。
myths.fact_en: Museum teaching pages say horizontal lines suggest rest and diagonal lines can give a feeling of movement. Those are common habits of seeing that artists use. They are not laws, and one picture can use the same kind of line in another way.
myths.fact_zh: 博物館的教學資料寫的是：水平線「讓人聯想到」休息，斜線「可以」帶來動的感覺。這些是常見的觀看習慣，藝術家會運用它們；但它們不是定律，同一種線在別的圖裡可以有別的用法。

myths.myth_en: Paul Klee wrote, “A line is a dot that went for a walk.”
myths.myth_zh: 保羅・克利寫過：「線是一個去散步的點。」
myths.fact_en: That is a popular short version. His book of 1925 begins, “An active line on a walk, moving freely, without goal,” and goes on to say that the mover is a point shifting its position forward.
myths.fact_zh: 那是流行的簡化版。他 1925 年的書開頭寫的是「一條主動的線在散步，自由地移動，沒有目的地」，接著才說推動它的是一個不斷往前移動的點。

myths.myth_en: A good line is perfectly smooth and the same width all the way.
myths.myth_zh: 好的線條，就是從頭到尾一樣粗、完全平滑。
myths.fact_en: An even line is one choice among many. Artists change a line from thick to thin, hard to soft, and dark to light on purpose, and in baimiao those changes are what show weight and movement.
myths.fact_zh: 均勻的線只是眾多選擇之一。藝術家會刻意讓線由粗變細、由硬變軟、由深變淺；在白描裡，正是這些變化表現出重量和動態。

tricks.title_en: A line is a point that moved
tricks.body_en: Every line is the path of something that traveled.
tricks.body_zh: 每一條線，都是某個東西走過的路。

tricks.body_en: Press harder for a thicker line, and lift for a thinner one.
tricks.body_zh: 壓重一點線就粗，提起來線就細。

tricks.title_zh: 平的像休息，斜的像在動
tricks.body_en: Horizontal lines suggest rest and diagonals suggest movement. These are suggestions, not rules.
tricks.body_zh: 水平線讓人聯想到休息，斜線讓人聯想到動。這是聯想，不是規則。

tricks.body_en: Close parallel lines are hatching, and crossed ones are cross-hatching.
tricks.body_zh: 排得很密的平行線是細線法；交叉起來就是交叉線法。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Carry pencils and brushes with the point down, and do not walk around with one in your mouth.
safety.zh: 拿著鉛筆或毛筆走動時，筆尖朝下；不要把筆含在嘴裡走路。

safety.en: Cover the desk before you use ink or markers, and keep ink away from books and screens. Wash brushes and hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 用墨汁或粗筆之前先把桌面鋪好，墨汁要離書本和螢幕遠一點。畫完把筆和手洗乾淨。

safety.en: Put the caps back on markers. Use markers made for school, and open a window if the smell is strong.
safety.zh: 粗筆用完要蓋回筆蓋。請用學校用的筆；味道太重就打開窗戶。

safety.en: Rest your eyes when you draw on a screen: ten minutes after every thirty minutes of close work.
safety.zh: 在螢幕上畫圖也要讓眼睛休息：用眼每 30 分鐘休息 10 分鐘。

materials.en: A soft pencil and white paper
materials.zh: 一支軟的鉛筆和白紙

materials.en: A brush with ink or dark watercolor, and paper that can take water
materials.zh: 一支毛筆，加上墨汁或深色水彩，以及吸水的紙

materials.en: A watch or a timer
materials.zh: 手錶或計時器

materials.en: This page, with the five lines on the left
materials.zh: 這一頁，左邊的五種線

steps.en: Watch the five lines on the page. For each one, write down two words that describe it.
steps.zh: 看頁面上的五種線。每一種各寫下兩個形容它的詞。

steps.en: With the pencil, draw the same wavy line five ways: light and steady, heavy, as fast as you can, with a shaky hand, and from heavy to light.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆把同一條波浪線畫五次：輕而穩、重、盡量快、手抖著畫、由重到輕。

steps.en: Do the same with the brush. Time the slow line and the fast line.
steps.zh: 用毛筆再畫一次這五種線。替慢的那一條和快的那一條計時。

steps.en: Look at your fast brush line. Does it have gaps? Load the brush with more ink and try again. Then try with less.
steps.zh: 看看你用毛筆很快畫的那一條：上面有空隙嗎？讓筆多沾一點墨再畫一次；然後少沾一點再畫一次。

steps.en: Compare your ten lines with the five on the screen. Where does the model match your paper, and where does it not?
steps.zh: 把你的十條線和螢幕上的五條比一比。模型和紙上的結果，哪裡一樣？哪裡不一樣？

activities.tip_en: On this page a fast stroke always leaves gaps. On paper you may find that a brush full of ink leaves none however fast you go, and a nearly dry brush leaves them even when you go slowly. That difference is worth writing down.
activities.tip_zh: 在這一頁，畫得快就一定有空隙。在紙上你可能會發現：吸飽墨的筆不管畫多快都沒有空隙，而快乾掉的筆就算慢慢畫也有。這個差別值得記下來。

activities.title_en: Shade a Ball with Lines Only
activities.title_zh: 只用線條替一顆球畫上明暗

materials.en: A sharp pencil or a fine pen, and white paper
materials.zh: 一支削尖的鉛筆或細字筆，和白紙

materials.en: A ruler
materials.zh: 一把尺

materials.en: Lesson 3 of this series, open at the model of the ball
materials.zh: 本系列第三課，停在那顆球的模型

steps.en: Draw a row of four boxes. Leave the first one empty.
steps.zh: 畫一排四個格子，第一格留白。

steps.en: Fill the second box with thin parallel lines set far apart, and the third with lines set close together.
steps.zh: 第二格畫上細細的平行線，排得疏一點；第三格的線排得密一點。

steps.en: In the fourth box, draw close lines and then cross them with a second set. You now have four values made of lines alone.
steps.zh: 第四格先畫密密的線，再用另一組線和它交叉。現在你有四階只用線條做出來的明度。

steps.en: Draw a circle. Use your four boxes as a guide to shade it like the ball in Lesson 3, with no smudging: open paper toward the light, crossed lines in the darkest band.
steps.zh: 畫一個圓。照著這四格，替它畫上像第三課那顆球的明暗，不要用手抹：朝著光的地方留白，最暗的那一圈用交叉的線。

steps.en: Hold the drawing at arm's length. Do the lines blend into gray? Step back until they do, and measure how far that is.
steps.zh: 把畫拿到一隻手臂遠的地方看。線條有沒有融成一片灰？一直往後退，退到融成灰為止，量量看那是多遠。

activities.tip_en: Keep the lines in each box the same weight and change only how close they are. If your hatching follows the curve of the ball, the ball will look rounder. Try it both ways and compare.
activities.tip_zh: 同一格裡的線要一樣粗，只改變它們的疏密。如果你的線順著球面彎，球看起來會更圓。兩種畫法都試試，再比較。
